stories.title: Woman constable dies after consuming poison:Posted at Saifai police station in Etawah; had argument with husband over returning home late after duty
stories.summary: After a dispute with her husband over being late returning home in Etawah, a female constable consumed a poisonous substance on Sunday evening. As her condition worsened, her family took her to Saifai Medical College, where she died around 10 PM during treatment. The husband stated- In the evening, he had angrily left the house. A while later, his wife called, but he did not respond. When he returned home around 7:30 PM, he saw his wife lying unconscious. The incident occurred at the residential complex located in the Police Line. The deceased has been identified as Priyanka (30), a resident of Saharanpur. She was recruited into the UP Police in 2019 and was currently posted at Saifai Police Station in Etawah. Argument over coming late Woman constable Priyanka had an arranged marriage with Rajat in 2023. Rajat is unemployed and lives with his wife in the police line. They have a one-and-a-half-year-old daughter and a six-month-old son. According to family members, Priyanka was on duty at Saifai police station. Her duty ended at 3 PM on Sunday. After that, she went shopping at the Sunday market. After shopping, she reached her quarter in the police line around 5:30 PM. Priyanka's husband Rajat also lived with her in the quarter. He asked the reason for her delay. She said she had gone to the market, but her husband did not believe her. Rajat asked why he was not informed about it earlier. An argument broke out between the two over this. Around 6:15 pm, Rajat angrily left the house. Priyanka called him many times, but he did not answer the phone. Foam was coming out of her mouth Rajat told the police that when he returned home around 7:30 pm, Priyanka was lying unconscious on the ground. Foam was coming out of her mouth. With the help of neighbors, she was immediately taken to the district hospital. Due to her critical condition, doctors referred Priyanka to Saifai Medical College. She died here around 10 pm during treatment. Husband taken into custody for questioning Upon receiving information about the incident, senior police officers including SSP Brijesh Kumar Srivastava and Civil Lines Kotwali Station Incharge K.K. Mishra reached the spot with police force. Police took husband Rajat into custody and interrogated him. The body has been sent for post-mortem. Civil Lines Kotwali Station Incharge K.K. Mishra said- Woman constable Priyanka committed suicide in the police line quarter. Initial investigation suggests she consumed a poisonous substance after a dispute with her husband. Family members are being questioned. The actual cause of death will be clear only after the post-mortem report.

stories.title: Mayawati's attack on BJP-AAP:Raises issues from Ravidas Gurughar wall demolition to unemployment, says ‘Govts focus on profiteering instead of public welfare’
stories.summary: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati criticised the BJP and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) for allegedly politicising the name of Sant Ravidas. She said that when the holy Gurughar of Santguru Ravidas in Tughlakabad, Delhi, was demolished on August 10, 2019, the AAP was in power. Similarly, the government that demolished the wall of the Gurughar in Dhaleta village, Punjab, was also the AAP government, she said. In protest, members of the community across the country took to the streets democratically but had to face lathi charges, tear gas, arrests and legal cases. She said many people were also jailed during the movement. Now that elections are approaching, the AAP and BJP are organising various programmes in the name of Sant Ravidas for political gain, she alleged. Even today, devotees are forced to bow their heads in a tin shed Mayawati said society needs to remain vigilant against the politics of both parties. She appealed to people to spread the message of Sant Guru Ravidas's ideals of respect, equality and justice among the masses. The BSP chief said the land belonging to the Gurughar was also taken away, and even today, devotees are forced to visit and bow before Guruji in a temporary iron-sheet shed. She said this situation hurts the sentiments of millions of devotees and remains etched in the community's memory. She alleged that, with the Punjab elections approaching, the BJP was trying to divert the community from the goal of Begumpura by organising a Kalash Yatra in the name of Santguru Ravidas. Meanwhile, in the case involving the demolition of the Gurughar wall in Dhaleta village, Punjab, arrests were made when the Sangat and BSP raised their voices, she said. According to Mayawati, the AAP government later had to bow to pressure and rebuild the Gurughar. She appealed to society to remain vigilant against the politics of the BJP and AAP. She also called upon the Sangat to participate in the 'End of Subjugation and Resolution of Begumpura Santguru Ravidas Samman Yatra'. Policy to provide work to every hand is necessary Mayawati also targeted the central and state governments over issues including unemployment, inflation, poverty, illiteracy, the healthcare system, migration, women's insecurity, paper leaks and corruption. She said that during its tenure in Uttar Pradesh, the BSP had created around 2.25 lakh new government posts in the police and Panchayati Raj departments. Along with this, by lifting the ban on recruitment, government jobs were provided to lakhs of people from all sections of society. Mayawati said that even after being out of power, the BSP had long been demanding that the central and state governments take effective steps to address issues such as inflation, extreme poverty, unemployment, illiteracy, the deteriorating healthcare system, backwardness, forced migration, women's insecurity, paper leaks and corruption. However, she said, governments were not showing the expected seriousness on these issues. Vacant posts in government departments should be filled immediately Referring to the movement by unemployed youth, Mayawati said educated young men and women had made issues such as unemployment and an uncertain future a subject of national debate through a 36-day protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. In view of these problems, she said the central and state governments should immediately take steps in the interests of the poor, labourers, youth, women and other hardworking people. She said governments would have to pay special attention to government employment. Along with stopping the process of selling national assets to private hands, time-bound recruitment, free from paper leaks and corruption, should be launched for millions of vacant posts across all government departments. Mayawati said that if even one member of a family secures a government job, it would directly benefit millions of families. According to her, this would also provide social and economic security to SC, ST and OBC communities, which has been weakened by the ineffective implementation of reservation. Governments should abandon the mindset of profiteering The BSP chief said all governments should abandon profiteering and a business-oriented approach focused on making profits, and honestly implement the humanitarian and welfare policies and principles of the Constitution. She said a policy of 'work for every hand' could help address millions of problems in the interests of the country and its people. CJP makes unemployment a subject of serious debate Mayawati praised the movement of the 'Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)'. She said the organisation had made burning issues such as unemployment a subject of serious debate of national importance. Educated young men and women, troubled by an uncertain future, staged a 36-day protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. Its impact was so widespread, she claimed, that even the country's Education Minister had to lose his position. She told the central and state governments that they should now immediately focus on the real problems faced by around 125 crore poor people, labourers, youth, women and other hardworking citizens of the country. In particular, she called for concrete steps to create employment opportunities and secure the future of young people, while prioritising the concerns of millions of families suffering from unemployment. She also demanded an end to the ongoing deadlock in the current session of Parliament over issues concerning protesting students and unemployed youth at Jantar Mantar. Mayawati said these issues should be properly debated and discussed in Parliament so that the practice of government Bills becoming laws without adequate discussion could be stopped.

stories.title: ₹26 lakh BMW superbike seized in Kashi:Rider revved it to sound like gunfire, pleaded with cops, ‘I made a mistake’
stories.summary: Varanasi Police seized a BMW superbike worth ₹26 lakh after its rider allegedly spent the past 10 days riding through roads, neighbourhoods and residential colonies while making firing-like sounds with a modified silencer. According to complaints, whenever someone passed by the biker, he would make a loud, explosion-like sound, frightening people. After receiving several complaints, police had been searching for the rider. Late on Sunday night, police were conducting checks near Englishia Line. During the operation, the youth approached on his bike while making loud noises. Police stopped him and took him to the police station. After being caught, the youth began apologising to the police. He said, “Sir, I made a mistake... I will not do it again.” The incident took place in the Sigra police station area. Now read the full case in detail... Bike bought 15 days ago The arrested youth has been identified as Shivang, son of Satish Chand Maurya, a resident of Manduadih. He told police that he had bought the BMW bike around 15 days ago. He then had its silencer modified. He also said that he had not yet received the bike's number plate. Complaints had been coming in for a week Sigra Police Station in-charge Shivakant Mishra said complaints had been coming in for around a week about an expensive bike being ridden at high speed in the area and its silencer producing firing-like sounds. Residents were being disturbed by loud, explosion-like noises late at night. Following the complaints, police began searching for the rider. On Sunday night, while conducting checks near Englishia Line, police stopped the youth and brought him to the police station. No number plate; silencer also modified The investigation found that the bike was manufactured by BMW and was worth around ₹26 lakh. It did not have a number plate. Its silencer had also been modified, causing it to produce loud, firing-like noises and sparks. During questioning, Shivang admitted his mistake and apologised to the police. He assured them that he would not repeat it. Youth says, 'I made a mistake, please forgive me' Sigra Police Station in-charge Shivakant Mishra said- The young man has admitted his mistake. The bike has been seized for violating the Motor Vehicles Act and pollution-related rules. The young man was released after the necessary legal action.

stories.title: CM Yogi leads Tiranga Yatra in Gorakhpur:Large crowd joins with flags; women, children participate, ‘Vande Mataram’ slogans raised
stories.summary: The Tiranga Yatra has started in Gorakhpur under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. The CM is walking on foot, holding the tricolor in his hand. A large number of people are also participating in the yatra with him. Great enthusiasm is visible among school children and women. Tricolors are being waved everywhere and 'Jai Shri Ram' slogans are echoing. Before the start of the yatra, the Chief Minister garlanded the statue of Mahatma Gandhi. After this, he joined the yatra holding the tricolor. The Chief Minister will walk about 3 kilometers. The yatra is now moving towards Yatayat Chauraha. Earlier, in his address, CM Yogi said, The tricolor is the mantra of freedom. He stated that it is the duty of every citizen to honor the brave heroes who made sacrifices. The CM also appealed to people to take the tricolor home and take selfies with it. The Chief Minister said that it is important to remember the contribution of the revolutionaries of the freedom movement. The tricolor is not just a flag, but the identity of the country's freedom and sacrifice.

stories.title: Huge crowd in Kashi, Mahakumbh-like arrangements:3 lakh devotees offer prayers; brother-in-law and sister-in-law die in Farrukhabad
stories.summary: Today is the second Monday of Sawan, and Shiva temples across Uttar Pradesh, including those in Varanasi, Ayodhya and Prayagraj, are witnessing huge crowds of devotees. Chants of ‘Har Har Mahadev’ can be heard across the state. Around 3 lakh devotees have so far had darshan of Baba Vishwanath. A 3-km-long queue has formed outside the temple. 3 lakh devotees visit Baba Vishwanath; 3-km queue outside temple ADCP Vaibhav Bangar said the Ganga Dwar has been closed due to the rising water level of the Ganga. This has led to larger crowds at the temple. As a result, arrangements similar to those made during the Maha Kumbh have been implemented. The lanes leading to the temple and ghats have been made one-way to manage the crowd. Devotees are getting only one second to perform Jalabhishek of Baba Vishwanath. On the second Monday of Sawan, Baba Vishwanath is giving darshan to devotees in his Gauri-Shankar form. The temple's CEO and SDM showered flower petals on devotees. The Baba Vishwanath Dham has been decorated with 50,000 flowers, while red carpets have been laid for devotees. Congress MP from Saharanpur, Imran Masood, showered flower petals on Kanwariyas. He also distributed fruit to them with his own hands and served them kheer. See pictures Two Kanwariyas killed after tractor-trolley runs them over in Barabanki In Barabanki, three young men travelling by motorcycle to Lodheswar Mahadeva temple for darshan were run over by a tractor-trolley. Two of them died, while the third suffered serious injuries. Kotwal Amit Singh carried the injured man in his arms to the vehicle and arranged for him to be taken to hospital. Devar-bhabhi killed in road accident while returning from Kanwar pilgrimage In Farrukhabad, a devar and his bhabhi died in a road accident late on Sunday night while returning from their Kanwar pilgrimage. The two were travelling by motorcycle to Mainpuri after collecting Ganga water for the Kanwar. A motorcycle suddenly collided with their bike, causing both of them to fall on the road. At the same time, a speeding pickup drove over their heads, killing them both.

stories.title: Abaan’s friends Umar, Zaid critical:One has ruptured lung, the other behaves strangely; Atiq’s son Ahzam recites Fateha at graves
stories.summary: Atiq's youngest son, Abaan, was laid to rest on Saturday, August 8, following his death in a road accident. The condition of his injured relatives, Umar and Zaid, has become critical. Umar was initially undergoing treatment at Ashutosh Hospital in Prayagraj. He has three broken ribs, fractures in his arms and legs, and severe lung problems. Doctors suspect that his lung has ruptured. On Saturday evening, when his condition deteriorated significantly, he was shifted to Medanta Hospital in Delhi. He underwent surgery on Sunday. The condition of the other injured person, Zaid, is also critical. His condition worsened on Sunday morning, after which he was taken to Delhi and shifted to the Military Hospital. Zaid has two broken ribs, a fractured arm and fractures in both legs, along with a wound near his neck. He also suffered a severe head injury and has been speaking incoherently and behaving unusually. Zaid was initially admitted to Aman Hospital in the city. On the doctors' advice, he was shifted to Delhi for further treatment for his brain injury. The condition of the third friend, Farooq Ahjam, who was travelling in the car, is stable. He suffered injuries to his hands and feet, along with minor wounds at several places. He has been admitted to Kareli Hospital. On the second day after Abaan's burial, brother Ahjam visits his grave On Sunday, Abaan's brother Ahjam once again visited his brother's grave and offered Fatiha. Relatives and friends were also present with him. Ahjam offered Fatiha not only at Abaan's grave, but also at the graves of his father Atiq, brother Asad and uncle Ashraf. Among Muslims, family members traditionally visit a grave to recite Fatiha on the second and third days after burial. They then visit after Friday prayers and recite Fatiha again on the 40th day. Ahjam spends time at his aunt's house and in the mosque A mournful atmosphere prevailed in Hatwa after Abaan's burial. On Sunday, people continued arriving from morning until evening to meet Ahjam and offer condolences to the family. Ahjam spent most of his time at his aunt's house or in the mosque. The village's main mosque is only around 100 metres from the house where Abaan's body had been kept. Ahjam would sit at home with friends and relatives before going to the mosque, where he would spend time. People who came to meet and console him also met him at the mosque. Ashraf's daughters call out to Ali and Umar, but police stop them from meeting On Saturday, Ali, who is lodged in Jhansi jail, and Umar, who is lodged in Prayagraj jail, arrived on parole to attend the funeral of their younger brother Abaan. During the burial at Kasari Masari cemetery, members of the Atiq family appeared emotional in the presence of Umar, Ali and Ahjam. At one point in the cemetery, three children of their late uncle Ashraf stood as the funeral procession passed. When Umar and Ali walked a few steps away, Ashraf's 12-year-old daughter Swaliha called out, "Brother." Umar and Ali recognised her voice in the crowd and suddenly stopped. Swaliha was with her 10-year-old younger sister Alia and seven-year-old brother Abdullah. Umar quickly picked Abdullah up in his arms. Both brothers kissed his forehead. Meanwhile, as the two girls began moving towards Umar and Ali, police stopped them. An IPS officer told them, “Meet only according to the High Court's order.” Umar told the policemen, "Hey, she's my little sister." However, the police replied, "No... meeting everyone is not allowed." Umar and Ali became emotional. Their sisters also began crying, but the police did not allow them to meet. Ali gets angry at police restrictions; Umar calms him down Another emotional moment occurred at Kasari Masari cemetery when Ali became angry over the police restrictions. Umar immediately hugged him and calmed him down. After Abaan's burial, Umar and Ali put soil on the grave. The police then asked Ali to move away. Ali loudly said, "Hey, let us recite the Fatiha!" Seeing Ali become angry, the crowd also began making noise. Umar immediately hugged him and said, “Have patience... be quiet.” As the crowd grew louder, Umar put his finger to his lips and signalled everyone to remain silent. Abaan was travelling to Jhansi jail to meet his brother when he died in road accident Abaan died in a road accident in Jhansi on Thursday morning, August 6. He was travelling from Prayagraj to meet his brother Ali, who is lodged in Jhansi jail. He was travelling in a Creta car with four friends. At around 10.30am, the car hit a divider on the highway while the driver was trying to avoid an animal. Abaan and his friend Sonu died in the accident, while three others were injured. The bodies of Abaan and Sonu were brought from Jhansi to Hatwa village in Prayagraj in the same ambulance at around 4am on Friday. Abaan was laid to rest at 7pm on Saturday, August 8. Was travelling with friends and relatives to meet Ali in jail Sonu, who died alongside Abaan, was his friend and a resident of Hatwa. He regularly spent time with Abaan and the others as a close friend. Umar, who was injured in the accident, is also a resident of Hatwa and a close relative of the Atiq family. After the houses in Chakia were demolished, Abaan, Ahjam and other family members began living at Umar's house in Hatwa. Umar was regularly with Abaan and Ahjam. Farooq, who was injured, was a friend of Ahjam and Abaan. He is a resident of Mohatsiganj. His father, Mohammad Farooq, worked in the office of Atiq's PA. He has also previously been jailed. Mohammad Zaid, who was injured, is a relative of Atiq. He is the son-in-law of Atiq's sister and was also regularly with Ahjam and Abaan.

stories.title: Ram Mandir donation theft case:Champat Rai back in race for general secretary post after VHP's clean chit, seers' backing
stories.summary: Champat Rai, who resigned as general secretary of the Ram Mandir Trust after allegations surfaced in connection with the alleged theft of temple donations, is once again being considered for the post. According to sources, Rai was given a clean chit at the Vishva Hindu Parishad's (VHP) national meeting in Delhi on July 22. The following day, several prominent seers in Ayodhya held a meeting in his support and demanded that he be reappointed as general secretary. Since then, Rai has been meeting seers and mahants regularly. He has been visiting temples, discussing the management of the Ram Temple and seeking to rebuild confidence in his leadership. Seers: If investigation clears Rai, he should return Swami Rajkumar Das, head of Ramvallabhakunj and a member of the Ram Mandir's religious committee, said Rai was considered innocent by the seer community. "If he is cleared in all the investigations, it would be welcome if he is appointed general secretary again," Das said. He said Rai's return would help strengthen the management of the Ram Temple and serve the interests of the Sanatan community. Das also highlighted Rai's contribution to the Ram Mandir movement and its construction, both alongside the late Ashok Singhal and after his death. Seers met in Ayodhya a day after VHP meeting The VHP held its national meeting in Delhi on July 22. The following day, on July 23, prominent seers from Ayodhya gathered at the Tulsidas Naturopathy Hospital premises of the Maniram Das Chhawani Trust. The meeting was held in support of Rai. Those present included Mahant Kamal Nayan Das, Swami Rajkumar Das, Mahant Mithilesh Nandini Sharan, Akhara Parishad spokesperson Mahant Sanjay Das, Vaishnav Akhara Parishad spokesperson Mahant Gaurishankar Das, Tulsidas Chhawani Mahant Janardan Das and Ramkachahari Mahant Shashikant Das, among others. During the meeting, the seers highlighted Rai's contribution to the Ram Mandir movement and described the allegations against him as a conspiracy. They also called for his reappointment as general secretary of the Ram Mandir Trust. Rai's supporters seek backing from seers Sources said people close to Rai had approached seers and mahants at various temples and sought their support for him. The sources claimed the atmosphere changed after the campaign for his support gained momentum. They also said opposition to Rai within the VHP eased after signals from senior leadership. The seers subsequently focused on Rai's contribution to the Ram Mandir movement and described the allegations against him as an alleged conspiracy. Rai's supporters have also pointed to his age of 81 and claims that he does not maintain bank accounts. According to people close to him, Rai is also planning to give up his share of his ancestral property. They said this is his only property and that he may soon transfer it to his brother through a legal registration. No decision on September 2 expected Rai could be given charge of the Ram Mandir Trust's general secretary post again within the next two to three months, according to sources. The Trust had deferred the appointment at its July 19 meeting. Its next meeting is scheduled for September 2. However, sources said the Trust is unlikely to take a final decision on the general secretary's post at that meeting either. Acting general secretary Krishnamohan also active Meanwhile, acting general secretary Dr Krishnamohan has stepped up his activities. He has been visiting the Ram Mandir to review its arrangements and holding discussions with members of the religious committee to improve its functioning. Six days ago, he visited the Ayodhya branch of the State Bank of India to review the Trust's bank accounts and locker arrangements. Bajrang Lal Bagda also in contention VHP international general secretary Bajrang Lal Bagda is also being discussed as a possible candidate for the post. Bagda was appointed international general secretary of the VHP in February 2024. As a result, Rai and Bagda are currently the two names being discussed for the general secretary's position. Rai observing silence during Chaturmas Amid the allegations linked to the donation theft case, Rai is staying at the Teerth Kshetra Bhawan in Ayodhya and observing a period of silence during Chaturmas. Sources claim that efforts could be made to restore his reputation after the vow ends. The authorities are currently awaiting the final report of the Special Investigation Team (SIT), which is investigating the alleged donation theft. Meanwhile, Rai has remained in Ayodhya and continues to express his views on decisions related to the Trust, according to sources. Eight arrested on June 25; Rai resigned the next day Rai and Ram Temple Trust trustee Dr Anil Mishra resigned on June 26 in connection with the donation theft case. The first FIR was registered late on June 25 following a complaint by Trust member Krishna Mohan. The FIR did not name Rai, Mishra or other senior Trust officials. Later that night, eight people, including Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu, were arrested.

stories.title: Why do Samajwadi Party Congress want to weaken Owaisi?:AIMIM got twice the votes of SP candidates' losing margins on several 2022 UP seats
stories.summary: With six months to go before the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, Asaduddin Owaisi's All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) has started strengthening its presence in Muslim-dominated areas of western UP. Over the past one-and-a-half months, Owaisi has held four major rallies in Bahraich, Bijnor, Saharanpur and Moradabad — areas traditionally considered strongholds of the Samajwadi Party (SP) among Muslim voters. Muslim MLAs from the SP represent these areas. The crowds at Owaisi's rallies and his aggressive speeches have raised concerns within opposition parties, particularly the SP. The SP and Congress are now reportedly trying to bring influential Muslim leaders from AIMIM into their camps. AIMIM diverted Muslim votes from SP in 2022 AIMIM contested 97 of Uttar Pradesh's 403 Assembly seats in the 2022 elections and secured a vote share of 0.49%. Although its statewide vote share was small, the party secured between 5,000 and 25,000 votes in several constituencies where it had focused its campaign. In at least seven to eight seats, the SP's losing margin was significantly smaller than the number of votes secured by AIMIM candidates. In other words, had AIMIM not contested those seats, or had some of its votes gone to the SP, the party could have won several of these closely fought contests. Who are the AIMIM leaders on SP-Congress radar? National spokesperson Asim Waqar leads the list AIMIM national spokesperson Asim Waqar has recently appeared to take a softer position towards the INDIA bloc and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. During a television debate, he described Rahul Gandhi as a potential future Prime Minister. He also responded to attacks on SP chief Akhilesh Yadav by Om Prakash Rajbhar. When Dainik Bhaskar asked Waqar about his political future, he did not rule out the possibility of moving to another party, although he did not openly confirm any such plan either. SP in touch with AIMIM district presidents in western UP The SP and Congress are reportedly keeping an eye on AIMIM district presidents in Saharanpur, Moradabad, Rampur and Meerut. A switch by these leaders could potentially bring parts of their local organisational networks with them. Moradabad AIMIM district president Wasim Mohid Farghani said Owaisi himself had offered an alliance to the SP. "Our aim is to raise our voice against injustice faced by Muslims. However, I cannot say anything at present about whether I would join the SP or Congress in the future," he said. Rampur AIMIM district president Farid-uz-Zafar said the SP was giving representation to Muslims, but its representatives were unable to raise the community's concerns strongly. "Nobody knows what turn politics will take," he said. Saharanpur AIMIM district president Wasim said the party would contest the election strongly under Owaisi's leadership. "However, members of my family have previously been associated with the SP and Congress. Nobody knows what circumstances may arise in the future," he said. Owaisi takes aggressive line on Muslim issues, draws Gen Z crowds Jaigam Murtaza, who tracks Muslim politics in western UP, said Owaisi had hurt the SP's prospects in the 2022 Assembly elections. He said the SP lost several seats in Muslim-dominated constituencies by margins of 5,000 to 10,000 votes, where AIMIM candidates had divided the Muslim vote. In western UP, the SP-Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) alliance had expected a consolidation of Muslim and Jat votes. However, AIMIM candidates split the Muslim vote in several constituencies, allowing BJP-led candidates to win closely fought contests. Owaisi has become active six months ahead of the 2027 election. A significant number of young, including Gen Z voters, have attended his rallies. Murtaza said this was significant because both Akhilesh Yadav and Rahul Gandhi were trying to attract young voters. Owaisi has largely focused his rallies on Muslim-majority constituencies. He has accused the SP of taking Muslim votes but failing to take a strong stand on issues concerning Muslim leaders, including Azam Khan, and the wider community. AIMIM's political footprint in UP is growing Political analysts say AIMIM still faces several challenges in Uttar Pradesh, but its electoral footprint has expanded since it first contested the state Assembly election in 2017. The party fielded candidates in 38 constituencies in 2017 and secured a vote share of 0.24%. Its candidates, however, lost their deposits in most of the seats they contested. In the 2022 Assembly election, AIMIM contested around 95-97 seats and secured more than 450,000 votes. Its vote share rose to around 0.49%. The party has also made gains beyond Assembly elections. In the 2023 urban local body elections, AIMIM won five municipal or panchayat chairperson posts and 77 councillor seats. In the Meerut mayoral election, AIMIM's candidate came close to winning and finished second, ahead of the SP. The party's growing political presence has prompted both the SP and Congress to consider their strategies ahead of the 2027 election. What do SP and Congress say? SP: 'We welcome people with a secular ideology' SP spokesperson Azam Khan said the party would welcome AIMIM leaders if they shared its secular outlook. "If people with a secular ideology join us, they are welcome. We do not support politics based on any religion, whether it is Hindu or Muslim. Anyone who stands with the Constitution and social justice is welcome in the party," he said. He added that the SP would stand with anyone fighting against what he described as the exploitation of young people. Congress: 'It would be good if Asim Waqar joins' Congress spokesperson Surendra Rajput said the party would welcome AIMIM spokesperson Asim Waqar if he decided to join Congress. "Whether AIMIM leaders will join Congress is a matter for the party leadership to decide based on their suitability. If the leadership seeks our opinion about any leader, we will certainly give it," he said. Owaisi's four rallies and the SP's Muslim MLAs Bahraich — Matera Owaisi began his campaign on June 14 by announcing AIMIM state president Shaukat Ali as the party's Assembly candidate from Matera. SP's Maria Shah is the sitting MLA from the constituency. She is the wife of former minister Yasar Shah. Organisers claimed around 80,000 people attended Owaisi's rally. Bijnor — Najibabad At a 'Paigham-e-Ittehad' programme on June 29, Owaisi targeted the SP, BSP and Congress. SP's Tasleem Ahmed is the sitting MLA from Najibabad. Organisers claimed that around 80,000 to 100,000 people attended the rally. Saharanpur At his July 18 rally in Saharanpur, Owaisi raised issues ranging from Azam Khan's Jauhar University to Muslim political representation. The constituency has two SP Muslim MLAs, Ashu Malik and Umar Khan. His aggressive speech was followed by loud slogans from the crowd. Moradabad At the July 25 rally in Moradabad, organisers claimed that more than 50,000 people attended. It was here that Owaisi made an open offer of an alliance to the SP, saying it was time to talk now and warning the party not to regret the decision after the election. The SP has so far not held any talks with Owaisi over an alliance.

stories.title: Flood hits 40 villages in Farrukhabad, people sleep on roads:Families say lifetime savings destroyed; rain alert issued across UP’s 75 districts
stories.summary: Rainfall in the hills has caused 10 rivers, including the Ganga and Yamuna, to swell across Uttar Pradesh. In Farrukhabad and Bijnor, Ganga water is flowing over the highways, while several roads have been submerged. Around 40 villages are in the grip of flooding, with dozens of villages cut off and turned into islands. Residents have been forced to leave their villages and homes and live in tents along the roads. Many are also being forced to sleep on the roads at night. In Farrukhabad, 21 houses have already been swallowed by the Ganga. Residents are demolishing other houses that have come under threat from riverbank erosion themselves, so they can salvage materials such as bricks and steel rods and reuse them to rebuild their homes once the situation improves. Women broke down in tears as they watched their houses being demolished. Crying, they said, 'We built our home by saving every penny, but the flood has destroyed our life's earnings. Where will we go now?' Yamuna reaches ghat steps in Mathura; routes submerged in Vrindavan The water level of the Yamuna has reached the steps of the ghats in Mathura. The parikrama route at Keshi Ghat has been submerged in Vrindavan. Devotees are wading through around one foot of water to complete the parikrama. Around 25 km from Kanpur city, the water level of the Ganga has reached the Brahmavart Ghat. At the 'Brahma Ki Khunti' temple, the khunti has been submerged. Ganga water has reached Manikarnika Ghat in Kashi. The routes connecting all 84 ghats have been submerged. Flood hits Saharanpur after heavy rain; Delhi-Yamunotri Highway submerged Meanwhile, Saharanpur received such heavy rainfall on Monday that the Gangarav River suddenly went into spate. The bridge built over the river was damaged. River water began flowing over the Delhi-Yamunotri Highway. Three to four feet of water accumulated on roads and in residential colonies. Water also entered homes and shops, while cars and motorcycles were half-submerged. Rain alert issued for all 75 districts; heavy rain possible in Lalitpur and Mahoba The Meteorological Department has issued a rain alert for all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh today. Heavy rain is possible in Lalitpur and Mahoba. Compared with last year, the state has received 136 mm less rainfall since June 1. By August 9 last year, Uttar Pradesh had received 437 mm of rain, which was 2% above normal. This year, the state has received 341 mm so far, which is 20% below normal. See photos of rainfall and floods- Monsoon to remain more active in southern UP for next three days Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said- The low-pressure area that had formed over south-western Uttar Pradesh has now weakened. The monsoon trough is extending from Delhi and Agra towards the east-central Bay of Bengal. In addition, another low-pressure area formed over south West Bengal and adjoining northern Odisha is moving north-westwards. In such a situation, the monsoon will remain more active in the southern parts of Uttar Pradesh over the next three days.

Past election trends show that governments in Uttar Pradesh can be made or unmade by relatively small differences in vote share. If even 3-5% of Gen Z voters shift their preference, it could have a major impact on the electoral outcome. The BJP, Samajwadi Party (SP), Congress and Chandrashekhar Azad's party are all working on strategies to win over young voters. Here is a look at how small differences in vote share have translated into large differences in seats in previous elections, and what political parties are doing to attract Gen Z. 3.24% higher vote share gave SP a majority in 2012 The 2012 Assembly election saw a direct contest between the Samajwadi Party and the Bahujan Samaj Party. The SP secured 29.15% of the vote, just 3.24 percentage points more than the BSP's 25.91%. Yet, that relatively small difference translated into a huge gap in seats. The SP won 224 seats, while the BSP managed only 80 — a difference of 144 seats. The BJP secured around 15% of the vote and won 47 seats. 7.22% more votes gave NDA 148 extra seats in 2022 The 2022 Assembly election produced a similar pattern. The BJP-led NDA secured 43.82% of the vote and won 273 seats. The SP-led alliance received 36.60% of the vote and won 125 seats. A difference of 7.22 percentage points in vote share therefore translated into a gap of 148 seats. Gen Z could influence the outcome in 80-120 seats The recent mobilisation of Gen Z has increased political parties' focus on this voter group. Uttar Pradesh has around 13 crore voters, of whom an estimated 2.07 crore, or 15%, belong to Gen Z. If even a substantial section of these voters votes as a single bloc, they could potentially influence the outcome in 80-120 Assembly constituencies. In the 2022 Assembly election, 99 seats were decided by margins ranging from 1,000 to 10,000 votes. The BJP won 55 of these seats and the SP 35. The Rashtriya Lok Dal won three, while the NISHAD Party and Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party won two each. The Congress and BSP won one seat each. Young voters pose a major challenge for ruling BJP Sanjay Singh, an office-bearer of the Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR), which analyses election data, said Gen Z voters would remain a major challenge in the 99 seats won by margins of less than 10,000 votes in the 2027 election. "The BJP is in power, so the challenge before it is how effectively it can connect with young voters," he said. Singh also pointed to a decline in support for the BJP among young voters over successive elections. According to his research, around 85% of young voters supported the BJP in the 2014 Lok Sabha election. The figure fell to around 70% in 2019 and further to 50-55% in 2024. He said this represented a decline of around 30-35 percentage points in three elections. Gen Z makes its own political choices Lucknow-based educationist Pankaj Agrawal said Gen Z does not have an established political leader or party and is instead heavily influenced by Instagram and wider social media trends. Thousands of young people took to the streets to protest issues such as the NEET paper leak and new UGC rules, showing that they were willing to raise concerns about their future without relying on political parties, he said. Agrawal also pointed to protests at Jantar Mantar, where young people from families that support the BJP or the RSS also joined demonstrations against government policies. "This shows that young people can make political choices independent of their family's views," he said. How political parties plan to win over Gen Z BJP and RSS plan direct engagement with young voters Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath is expected to hold direct interactions with Gen Z voters. Students pursuing professional courses at different universities will be invited to participate. The proposed interactions will be two-way, with students also getting an opportunity to ask questions and raise their concerns with the Chief Minister. The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) has divided Uttar Pradesh into two regions — east and west. Regional RSS functionaries will visit universities to interact with Gen Z, understand their concerns and assess their expectations. The findings from these interactions will be shared with the government and BJP organisation to help shape their future strategy. BJP plans youth advisory committees The BJP also plans to create "Youth Advisory Committees" to establish a direct channel between young people and the government. The committees will include youth representatives, student leaders, competitive-exam aspirants, young entrepreneurs and social-media influencers. The initiative will initially operate at district level, with plans to expand it to the block level. The aim is to ensure that issues affecting young people reach MLAs and the government directly. BJP trains leaders to connect through social media The BJP is also training its representatives and leaders to communicate with young voters through reels, social media trends and X. The objective is to receive quick feedback on issues such as employment and competitive examinations and communicate the party's position directly to young people. SP focuses on influencers and young MPs Akhilesh meets more than 200 influencers SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has held a meeting with more than 200 digital content creators and influencers from across Uttar Pradesh. The party wants to reduce its dependence on traditional media and reach young voters directly through YouTube, Instagram and Facebook. The strategy includes providing influencers with data and facts on issues such as paper leaks, unemployment and inflation so they can create content around them. The party also plans to use local languages and dialects to connect with young people in rural areas and small towns. For the 2027 election, the SP is planning a dedicated digital war room to coordinate with content creators and build support for the party online. SP promotes its young MPs SP MPs Pushpendra Saroj and Priya Saroj, among the youngest MPs in the party, are also being promoted heavily on social media. Reels and short videos highlighting their speeches and comments on youth-related issues such as Agniveer, student protests and paper leaks are being circulated. Short documentaries focusing on their struggles and political journeys are also being shared to help first-time voters connect with them. Congress plans direct youth outreach Rahul Gandhi to hold more youth interactions Rahul Gandhi interacted with students in Prayagraj on August 8 as part of the party's youth outreach programme. Congress spokesperson CP Rai said around 1.74 lakh students had registered online for the "Goonj" programme. He said Rahul Gandhi is expected to hold similar interactions in two to three more districts of Uttar Pradesh. NSUI and Youth Congress to expand membership The Congress is also planning dedicated programmes to bring more Gen Z voters into the party. According to the party spokesperson, its Uttar Pradesh in-charge will interact with young people in different districts. The party has also asked its youth organisations, the National Students' Union of India (NSUI) and Youth Congress, to focus on expanding membership in colleges and universities. Social media could decide the youth vote Gen Z is less likely to be influenced by traditional rallies and political speeches and more likely to respond to the social-media environment around an issue. For political parties, the challenge is therefore not simply to reach young voters but to address the issues that directly affect them — employment, competitive examinations, education, inflation and their future prospects. The party that gets this balance right could gain a crucial advantage in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election.

stories.title: UP Madrasas to lose Kamil and Fazil degree status:Existing qualifications also to be invalidated; Yogi cabinet set to clear 21+ proposals tomorrow
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government is set to prohibit madrasas from awarding Kamil (graduate-level) and Fazil (postgraduate-level) degrees, saying the move is in line with a Supreme Court ruling. A proposal to amend the Uttar Pradesh Madrasa Education Board Act, 2004 will be placed before the Yogi Adityanath Cabinet at its meeting on Tuesday. Minority Welfare Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar said- Kamil and Fazil degrees previously awarded by madrasas will also be invalidated. Decision based on SC ruling A senior official from the Minority Welfare Department said the proposal follows the Supreme Court's judgment of 5 November 2024 in the Anjum Qadri and Others vs Union of India case. The Supreme Court overturned the Allahabad High Court's earlier ruling, which had declared the Uttar Pradesh Madrasa Education Board Act, 2004 unconstitutional. While upholding the constitutional validity of the Act, the apex court clarified that madrasas cannot award formal higher education qualifications such as Kamil and Fazil, as these fall outside the regulatory framework of the University Grants Commission (UGC). Cabinet to meet on Tuesday; 21 proposals on Agenda The Cabinet meeting will be held at 9.30 am on Tuesday at the Chief Minister's official residence. Chief Secretary S.P. Goyal released the agenda on Monday evening, listing 21 proposals, with the possibility of additional items being added before the meeting. The Cabinet is also expected to consider a supplementary Budget exceeding ₹40,000 crore for the 2026–27 financial year. What are Kamil and Fazil degrees? Kamil A three-year course in Arabic, Persian and Islamic studies. Previously treated by the Madrasa Board as equivalent to a Bachelor's degree (BA). Fazil A two-year advanced course undertaken after Kamil. Previously treated as equivalent to a Master's degree (MA). U-Hubs Proposed for Lucknow and Noida The Cabinet is also expected to approve the establishment of U-Hubs in Lucknow and Noida. According to the Information Technology and Electronics Department, the state government has recently approved the creation of a Startup Mission Directorate. As part of this initiative, a government-owned company named U-Hub will be established. The centres will be developed at IIT Kanpur's Noida Centre and the IIT Lucknow campus. The primary objective is to provide infrastructure, mentoring and institutional support to technology startups looking to scale their businesses. The government has allocated ₹100 crore for the initiative during the current financial year. The Director of IIT Kanpur Incubation Centre has also been appointed Director of U-Hub for a three-year term. Other key proposals before the cabinet The Cabinet is also expected to consider approval of the Sheera Policy 2026, implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana for Kharif and Rabi crops, and the creation of the Prayagraj–Chitrakoot Regional Development Authority for the integrated development of the region. Main agenda items Crop insurance schemes: Approval for implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana and the Weather-Based Crop Insurance Scheme for Kharif 2026 and Rabi 2026–27. Seven multi-purpose hubs: The Public Works Department will acquire land and transfer it free of cost to the Housing and Urban Planning Department for construction of seven multi-purpose hubs. New service rules: Introduction of the State Property Department Service Rules, 2026. HCL Foundation agreement: Proposal to extend the government's partnership with the HCL Foundation for community development projects by another five years. Prayagraj–Chitrakoot Development Authority: Creation of a new authority for the planned development of the region. Nomadic Development Board: Formation of a board for the social and economic development of denotified, nomadic and semi-nomadic communities. Vishwakarma Shram Samman Yojana-2: Amendments to the scheme and inclusion of new provisions. Jewar Link Expressway: Proposal to construct a 74.467-km six-lane greenfield expressway connecting Jewar Airport with the Ganga Expressway. Molasses law amendment: Introduction of the Uttar Pradesh Molasses Control (Amendment) Bill, 2026. Labour Code Rules, 2026: Implementation of new labour regulations. Withdrawal of old legislation: Proposal to withdraw the Building and Other Construction Workers (Amendment) Bill, 2020 from the Central Government. Madrasa law amendment: Amendments to the Madrasa Education Board Act, 2004 in line with the Supreme Court judgment. Kamil and Fazil degrees: Formal recognition of these qualifications will be discontinued. Mining service rules: Implementation of the Department of Geology and Mining Service Rules, 2026. U-Hubs in Lucknow and Noida: Establishment of technology hubs focused on deep-tech and high-potential startups. Relief for electronics company: Proposal to extend the deadline for iQOO Solutions to commence its project. CAG reports: Presentation of several Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) reports relating to state finances, MGNREGA, the Jal Jeevan Mission and other departments. Supplementary Budget: Presentation of supplementary grants and the Appropriation Bill for the 2026–27 financial year.

stories.title: Dalit man urinates on Shiva idol:Says, 'Do whatever you can'; police pick him up from home two hours later
stories.summary: In Bulandshahr, a 55-year-old Dalit man urinated on a Shivling on the first Monday of Sawan. The accused said, ‘Do whatever you want to do’. A youth from the village made a video of him and made it viral on social media. The incident occurred around 7 AM. Police reached the village 4 hours after the video surfaced. The elderly man and the person who made the video were taken from their homes. A case has also been registered against both. Complete incident in 3 pictures He reached near the idol of Shiva built near the temple's spire. He told the young man, ‘Here, make a video.’ Read the full incident in sequence Shiva temple 35 years old Bohich village is located in Shikarpur police station area, about 25 km from the district headquarters. There is a 35-year-old Shiva temple here. A large idol of Lord Shiva is installed on the temple's roof. There are stairs to go to the temple's roof. Hari Prasad Kumar (55)'s house is 200 meters away from the temple. He is a mason. On Monday morning around 7 AM, he reached the temple. He went up the stairs and urinated near the feet of Lord Shiva's idol. His entire act was recorded on phone by Pappu (45), a resident of the same village. Accused said that what will you do? After urinating, Hari Prasad got up from there and said to Pappu, who was making the video, I peed, what will you do? Make the video viral. What can anyone do? About 2 hours after this incident, around 10 am, anger spread among the people of the village and surrounding areas. People expressed strong displeasure over this incident that occurred on the first Monday of Sawan and demanded strict action against the accused. Police reached village as soon as video went viral As soon as information about the video was received, Shikarpur police immediately swung into action. Around 12 PM, the police team reached the village and took accused Hariprasad and Pappu, who made the video, into custody and brought them to the police station. Police have started questioning both of them. SSP said - Strict action will be taken SSP Dinesh Kumar Singh stated that both accused have been taken into custody and are being interrogated. After investigating the matter, strict action will be taken based on evidence. He appealed to the public not to pay attention to rumors and to maintain peace. Police are also investigating what was the motive behind making the video viral. Was it planned? Also, it is being investigated whether any other person played a role in making the video viral on social media or not. After the incident, police surveillance has been increased in the village as a precautionary measure.

stories.title: Dog fights with Cobra to save owner's life, dies:Battles with snake for an hour in Ballia, scummbs to death after killing
stories.summary: A Labrador dog in Ballia sacrificed its life to save its owner's family from a cobra. Around 2 AM on Sunday night, the dog spotted a cobra outside the house. The cobra was hissing with its hood spread. After this, the dog started barking continuously. During this, the cobra attacked the dog. Then the dog also grabbed the cobra. The snake kept attacking, but the dog did not let go. The struggle between the two continued for about an hour, while the family members watched and made videos of this fight. Finally, the dog killed the cobra. However, in this fight, the dog also fell victim to the cobra's venom. After 30 minutes, the dog also died. A video of this entire incident has also surfaced. The incident is from the Belthara Road area. First, watch the dog-cobra fight Now know the full story Danish lived with his family in Ubhanv village. He runs a brick kiln. Danish had a Labrador dog named Tommy at his home for 8 years. On Sunday night, a cobra snake was trying to enter Danish's house. Tommy first spotted the cobra. After this, Tommy started barking continuously. Hearing Tommy's noise, Danish and his family also woke up. Meanwhile, Tommy himself confronted the cobra. According to Danish's family members, a fierce struggle ensued between Tommy and the snake for about an hour. Tommy severely gripped the cobra. The cobra also put all its might to escape from Tommy's clutches. In this sequence, the cobra bit Tommy several times. But, Tommy did not give up. He killed the cobra. Tommy also died half an hour after killing the cobra During the fight with the cobra, the effect of the poison rapidly increased in Tommy's body. Half an hour later, he also passed away. The family says that if Tommy hadn't shown bravery, the snake would have entered the house and bitten anyone. Tommy saved the entire family by sacrificing his life. Tommy had been living as a family member for the past 8 years. Every member of the family is deeply shocked by his death. On Monday, the family bid a tearful farewell to Tommy. Many family members became emotional while burying him.

stories.title: No bulldozer action on Jauhar University as of now:Moradabad Commissioner's Court halts demolition of 38 buildings after 2.5-hour hearing
stories.summary: No demolition action will be taken against the 38 buildings of Rampur's Jauhar University while the matter remains pending before the court. The order was issued by the court of Moradabad Divisional Commissioner Anjaneya Kumar Singh at 4.45 pm on Monday, following a hearing that lasted around two and a half hours. The next hearing has been scheduled for 10 August. Earlier stay on demolition order The Commissioner's Court had previously heard the matter on 27 July, when it stayed the demolition order issued by the Vice-Chairman of the Rampur Development Authority (RDA) and the District Magistrate against the university's 38 buildings. The next hearing was then fixed for 3 August. University challenged RDA order The university management filed an appeal before the Commissioner's Court on 20 July, challenging the demolition order issued by the RDA Vice-Chairman. The hearing was originally scheduled for 28 July. However, following the death of an advocate in Moradabad, the day was declared a day of mourning. As a result, the university's counsel, Junaid Ejaz, moved an application on 27 July, requesting an earlier hearing. The Commissioner accepted the application and stayed the demolition order. Jauhar Trust challenges demolition order Junaid Ejaz, counsel for Jauhar University, said the Rampur Development Authority had issued the demolition order on 15 July, prompting the university to file an appeal before the Commissioner's Court. According to Ejaz, Monday's hearing lasted for about one hour and 45 minutes, during which both sides presented detailed arguments. After hearing the submissions, the matter was reserved for orders. He further said the Commissioner had orally observed that no demolition would take place while the appeal remained pending. The Divisional Commissioner has also sought a response from the RDA on the issues raised in the appeal and may summon additional records, including approved building plans, from the university if required. RDA says only two buildings were approved RDA Vice-Chairman Ajay Kumar Dwivedi issued an order on 15 July, declaring 38 of the university's 40 buildings to be unauthorised and directing that they be demolished. According to the RDA, the Jauhar Trust had obtained approval for only two buildings, while construction plans for the remaining 38 buildings had never been sanctioned. As the university campus falls within the jurisdiction of the Rampur Development Authority, all construction is governed by RDA regulations. Government Lawyer: No written order yet Government counsel Dinesh Chauhan said both parties presented their arguments before the court on Monday. He said the university's lawyer argued on behalf of the institution, while he represented the state government. After hearing both sides, the court reserved its decision but had not yet issued any written order. Chauhan added that the court may pass a final order, seek additional reports or issue further directions, and all subsequent action would depend on the written order. He stressed that only a written judicial order has legal validity and that it would be inappropriate to draw conclusions based solely on oral observations until the court formally issues its decision.

stories.title: SP to donate ₹47,000 to Ram Mandir:Dimple Yadav counts cash in Parliament; Ayodhya MP displays bundle of notes, says 'This will not be stolen'
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) MPs staged a protest outside Parliament at Makar Gate over the alleged theft of offerings from the Ayodhya Ram Temple. During the demonstration, SP leaders collected donations from MPs belonging to the INDIA bloc. The donations were then counted in full public view. MP Ram Shiromani Verma counted the cash with assistance from Dharmendra Yadav, while Akshay Pratap recorded the names of donors in a register. Dimple Yadav oversaw the counting process, and Ayodhya MP Awadhesh Prasad supervised the exercise. A total of ₹47,100 was collected. Dharmendra Yadav said every rupee had been accounted for to ensure complete transparency. The money was then handed over to Awadhesh Prasad, who said the entire amount would be sent directly to the Ram Temple in Ayodhya. Understand the protest in 6 pictures- Awadhesh Prasad: 'Not a single penny will be stolen' Speaking to the media, Awadhesh Prasad displayed bundles of cash and said- This money will not be stolen. It is an offering for the temple of Lord Shri Ram. Every one of our MPs has contributed. I take full responsibility that not a single penny from this amount will be stolen. Earlier on Monday, both Houses of Parliament witnessed noisy scenes, forcing the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha to be adjourned for the entire day. Dimple Yadav targets BJP and RSS Dimple Yadav accused the BJP and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) of trying to impose their ideology on women. Referring to a recent protest movement, she claimed it had ended after assurances that no FIRs would be registered against students or young women. However, she alleged that cases were later filed, accusing the government of reneging on its promise and betraying the public. Questions raised over Ram temple donations Dimple Yadav also questioned the management of donations made to the Ram Temple. She asked where anonymous cash donations, precious metals and other offerings had gone, and which organisations were benefiting from them. She questioned why the government had not disclosed these details publicly and why members of the temple trust had not been removed despite the allegations. According to her, public confidence in the government had eroded, and the government was fully responsible for the alleged donation theft and land-related irregularities. SP distances itself from Pappu Yadav's protest The Samajwadi Party distanced itself from the separate protest staged by Independent MP Pappu Yadav inside the Parliament complex. SP MP Ram Gopal Yadav said- That was wrong. Saints have nothing to do with the alleged theft at the Ram Temple. It should not have happened. He added that the party would raise the alleged theft of temple donations inside Parliament, describing it as a serious issue. Pappu Yadav stages protest dressed as a Sadhu On the 10th day of the Monsoon Session, Independent MP Pappu Yadav arrived at Parliament dressed as a saffron-clad sadhu carrying a donation box. A symbolic street play was staged inside the Parliament complex to protest against the alleged theft of Ram Temple offerings. Pappu Yadav, dressed as a priest, sat on the ground while Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and several opposition MPs placed donations into the collection drive. During the protest, Pappu Yadav was also seen keeping some donated cash with himself instead of placing it in the donation box. He was also seen touching the feet of Ayodhya MP Awadhesh Prasad. FIR registered against Rahul Gandhi, Pappu Yadav and Awadhesh Prasad An FIR has been registered in Varanasi against Congress MP Rahul Gandhi, SP MP Awadhesh Prasad and Independent MP Pappu Yadav over the protest concerning the alleged theft of Ram Temple offerings. The complaint was filed by Jagadguru Balak Das, head priest of Patalpuri Math, at the Kotwali police station.

stories.title: Video|Pole falls on schoolgirl's head, dies within 3 seconds:Friend narrowly escapes; was returning home from local shop
stories.summary: A Class 9 student walking along a road in Hardoi dies within three seconds after an electric pole snaps and falls on her head. Her friend, who is walking beside her, hears the pole cracking and steps forward just in time, escaping unharmed. The girl remains trapped under the pole for about 25 seconds before passersby use bamboo to lift it and pull her out. However, she has already succumbed to her injuries. The incident occurs in Bhihgaon, Behta Gokul, at around 6:30 pm on Sunday, and CCTV footage of the accident emerges today. 2 visuals of the accident Understand the entire incident sequentially Ajay Shukla lives with his family in Bhigaon, under the Behta Gokul police station area. Besides his wife Sadhana, there are 6 children in the house. Among them, Ragini (14) was the second eldest. She was a class nine student at Chandrasen Singh Munni Devi Inter College. Pandey Kirana Store is about 200 meters away from Ragini's house. Here, on Sunday evening, a DCM truck arrived loaded with Gyandhara feed. The DCM driver was moving the vehicle forward to unload the goods. Just then, an overhead electricity cable got entangled in the DCM's angle. The wire was pulled with such force that the electricity pole bent towards the road and broke. Just then, Ragini came into its path. She had gone out with her friend Kamini to buy something from this very shop. What is visible in the video? Both friends were walking hand-in-hand. As soon as the wire stretched and the sound of the pole breaking came, Kamini screamed and let go of Ragini's hand, moving forward. Meanwhile, Ragini, out of fear, remained standing in her spot to save herself. In just three seconds, the pole broke and fell directly on her head. As soon as it came under pole, her head burst. After the accident, there was chaos at the spot. Fearing electrocution, people initially stood at a distance. After about 25 seconds, two people lifted the pole with the help of bamboo. One person pulled the student out from under the pole. As soon as the news of the accident was received, the student's family members rushed to the spot. Mother started crying The entire family was in a state of distress, crying inconsolably. Mother Sadhana started crying, clinging to her daughter's body. She kept saying that she had just sent her daughter to get some things. After the accident, hearing the commotion, the DCM driver abandoned the vehicle and fled the scene. The police sent the body for post-mortem. Station House Officer Markandey Singh said- Police are also including CCTV footage in the investigation. A complaint has been received from the family members. Action will be taken against the accused DCM driver.

Haryanvi dancers perform at BJP MLA's event in Mathura:Supporters shower cash on two performers; children were also present
stories.summary: Haryanvi dancers performed at an event linked to BJP MLA Meghshyam Singh in Mathura, where supporters were seen showering notes on the performers. Several videos of the programme surfaced on Monday, showing two dancers performing on stage. However, BJP District President Harishankar Yadav denied it was an official party or MLA event, claiming it had been organised by local residents. The programme was held on 1 August in Janu village, where Govardhan MLA Meghshyam Singh attended a foundation stone-laying ceremony for development projects worth around ₹2.5 crore. Haryanvi dancers Sanjana Chaudhary and Bhavna Bhati were invited to entertain the audience. See pictures of the Haryanvi dancer- Now know what is visible in the video- The foundation stone-laying ceremony was organised for development works worth approximately ₹2.5 crore in Janu village under the Govardhan Assembly constituency. As part of the event, two Haryanvi dancers performed on stage. The videos show large crowds, including men, women and children, watching the performances. DJ music, including songs with explicit lyrics, was played throughout the programme. At several points, members of the audience joined the dancers on stage, while children were also seen climbing onto the platform. Many attendees recorded the performances on their mobile phones. Foundation stones for the development works were visible in front of the stage, while several people were seen showering bundles of banknotes on the performers. MLA could not be contacted In this matter, an attempt was made to contact BJP MLA Meghshyam Singh to know his side, but it was not possible to speak with him. No reaction has come from his side either. Meanwhile, supporters of the MLA say that it was merely an entertainment program. It should not be viewed from a political perspective. Meanwhile, BJP Metropolitan President Harishankar Yadav Raju said, "This was not a party program. It must have been organized by local people. Neither the MLA nor party workers were present in it. I cannot say anything about what the local people did." People said - one should find some way to entertain oneself After the video surfaced, various reactions are being seen on social media regarding it. In the comment box of a video shared on a Facebook account named Rajesh Kumar Satyamev, a user wrote, "The MLA's heart must be appeased somehow." Meanwhile, another user wrote, "The MLA did not dance." Another user called it having a negative impact on the youth.

stories.title: Mother-son held hostage in broad daylight:Thieves loot jewellery worth lakhs and ₹15,000 cash at gunpoint in Kanpur
stories.summary: Armed robbers carried out a daylight burglary in Kanpur's Chakeri area on Monday, holding a woman and her 16-year-old son hostage at gunpoint before fleeing with jewellery worth lakhs of rupees and ₹15,000 in cash. The incident took place at around 12 noon at the home of Rachna Tripathi in C Block, Shyamnagar. The robbers allegedly threatened Tripathi and her son, Devansh, with firearms before ransacking the house and escaping with valuables. Following the incident, ADCP (East) Shiva Singh, Chakeri police and a forensic team reached the scene. Police have launched an investigation.

stories.title: Father kills daughter over marriage to soldier:Strangles her with dupatta in Agra, sends wife and son away; sits beside body
stories.summary: An honor killing has occurred in Agra. Here, a father strangled his 22-year-old daughter to death. The reason is that the daughter had a court marriage with an ITBP jawan. On Sunday night at 12 AM, the father beat his daughter in front of his wife and son, then strangled her with a chunari (scarf). After the incident, he sent his wife and son away and sat crying near the body himself. Meanwhile, hearing the screams, the police were called. When the police went inside, the daughter was lying on the floor in a pool of blood. When the police asked the accused father the reason for the incident, he confessed to the crime. He said - 4 months ago, his daughter had a love marriage against the family's wishes, which is why he killed her. Currently, the police have arrested him. The entire incident is from the Jaitpur police station area, 80 km away from the district headquarters. The victim's name is Ankita Sharma (24). Family lives in a rented house Vimal Sharma had been living in a rented house in Nahtauli village of Jaitpur for the past 15 years. Vimal worked at a shop. His family included his wife Sita, son Ankush, and daughter Ankita. Ankita had an affair with Amit Pachauri, a resident of the village. Amit is deployed as a soldier in ITBP. Both wanted to get married, but the family was not ready for it. Going against her family, Ankita had a court marriage with Amit 4 months ago, against her family's wishes. After the marriage, Amit returned to duty, while Ankita continued to live with her parents. Her family members were upset about her love marriage. According to the police, Vimal went to his daughter's room at 12 AM on Sunday night and assaulted her. During this, neighbors heard Ankita screaming and informed the police by dialing 112. When the police arrived at the scene, Ankita's body was found in the room. DCP East Abhishek Agarwal said- The body has been sent for post-mortem. The accused is being interrogated. Further action will be based on the investigation and post-mortem report.

stories.title: BJP's Tiranga Yatra to reach 20 lakh people:Processions across 110 Lucknow wards and 2,515 booths to promote patriotism and respect for the national flag
stories.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) will launch a large-scale Tiranga Yatra campaign in Lucknow from August 9. The campaign will cover all 110 wards, 25 mandals and 2,515 booths across the city. The party aims to reach around 20 lakh people through public outreach during the campaign. BJP workers will organise Tiranga Yatras, conduct door-to-door visits and inform people about the achievements of the Central and Uttar Pradesh governments. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will inaugurate BJP state vice-president Neeraj Singh, who is the state in-charge of the Tiranga Yatra campaign, said the formal launch will take place on August 9 under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. The main Tiranga Yatra will begin from the Chief Minister's residence at 5 Kalidas Marg and conclude at the Assembly (Lok Bhawan). Senior BJP leaders, public representatives, party workers and a large number of citizens will participate in the yatra. Will deliver government achievements to every household According to the BJP, workers will inform people about development projects, welfare schemes and major achievements of the Central and state governments since the BJP came to power at the Centre in 2014. The campaign will also spread the message of patriotism, national unity and respect for the Tricolour among citizens. Public Outreach Campaign at Every Booth After the main Tiranga Yatra, separate rallies will be organised across all 110 wards, 25 mandals and 2,515 booths in Lucknow. Workers at every booth will conduct door-to-door outreach and interact with local residents. The party aims to connect with around 20 lakh people through the campaign and further strengthen its organisation at the booth level. BJP has assigned responsibilities to office-bearers of all mandals and booths for the campaign.

stories.title: One call saves ₹5.12 lakh in Varanasi:₹5.64 lakh siphoned off in 30 minutes; funds frozen after complaint to 1930, FIR registered
stories.summary: A man from Kumbhapur village in Varanasi's Badagaon police station area became a victim of online fraud. Cyber criminals withdrew ₹5,64,197 from his bank account in six transactions within just half an hour. As transaction messages started arriving on his mobile phone, the victim informed his family members. Without wasting time, they immediately called the cyber helpline. After providing the required details, the team managed to put ₹5,12,495 on hold, bringing relief to the family. The entire matter is from last week The incident took place on July 27 when sudden transactions started from the bank account of Ramesh Singh, a resident of Kumbhapur village. Ramesh said the fraudsters first withdrew ₹50,000 from his account. After this, ₹49,470, ₹81,351 and ₹1 lakh were deducted in multiple transactions. As he continued receiving messages, the fraudsters made two more withdrawals before he could take any action. They transferred ₹2,14,376 and later another ₹69,000 from his account. After this, Ramesh informed his family members, who immediately called the cyber helpline number 1930. The cyber team contacted the bank after receiving the complaint and got ₹5,12,495 frozen, preventing further loss. Police register case, begin investigation On Sunday evening, Ramesh submitted a complaint at Badagaon police station, demanding action against the fraudsters. Police have registered a case against unidentified accused under Section 318(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Officials are collecting bank transaction details to trace the cyber criminals. Badagaon Station House Officer Praveen Kumar Singh said that if money starts getting deducted from a bank account without the account holder's knowledge, people should not panic and must immediately report it by calling 1930.

stories.title: BSP hunts for candidates in Gorakhpur:Eyes rival party hopefuls; focus on five seats
stories.summary: With the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections approaching, the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) has intensified its search for candidates in Gorakhpur. Alongside strengthening its organisation, the party is identifying winnable faces for every Assembly constituency. The BSP is also reaching out to leaders from other parties who are unlikely to secure tickets from their own organisations. Party functionaries said details of potential candidates from every Assembly seat are currently being collected. Once the names are shortlisted, the list will be sent to the party leadership in Lucknow. No final decision has yet been taken for any constituency in the district. The BSP is simultaneously working on organisational strengthening and election preparations in Gorakhpur. After appointing three district presidents over the past five years, the party has also undergone organisational changes. District president Santosh Kumar Jigyasu said the organisational work is almost complete and the focus has now shifted entirely to selecting Assembly candidates. He said several aspirants have emerged from every constituency and their profiles are being assessed before recommending the strongest and most electable names to the state leadership. Maximum focus on these seats The BSP is currently focusing on Chillupar, Sahjanwa, Bansgaon, Khajni and Pipraich Assembly seats. All these constituencies are currently represented by BJP MLAs. With leaders from both BJP and Samajwadi Party also seeking tickets, the BSP is keeping an eye on those who have a low possibility of getting nominations from their own parties. A party office-bearer said several leaders have been seeking tickets for multiple elections but have not received an opportunity. This time, many of them are preparing to contest at any cost. Senior BSP leaders are also in talks with several such leaders. BSP was strong in 2007 and 2012 The BSP has had a strong electoral presence in Gorakhpur in the past. In the 2007 Assembly elections, when the BSP formed the government in Uttar Pradesh, the party won the Chillupar, Bansgaon, Kaudiram and Pipraich seats in the district. The Kaudiram Assembly seat was later removed during delimitation. In the 2012 Assembly elections, the BSP again held four seats in the district — Sahjanwa, Chillupar, Bansgaon and Chauri Chaura. The party is now trying to repeat its earlier performance in the upcoming Assembly elections.

stories.title: AI to be taught in 41 polytechnic engineering branches:Syllabus updated across state institutes; new curriculum to take effect from upcoming session
stories.summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) will now be a compulsory subject for students pursuing three-year diploma engineering courses in government, aided and private polytechnic institutes across Uttar Pradesh. From the 2026-27 academic session, AI has been included in the syllabus of all 41 diploma engineering programmes. Students in the first and second semesters will study the subject to prepare for evolving technologies. Updated syllabus will be implemented from new session Dr F.R. Khan, Director of the Institute of Research, Development and Training (IRDT), Kanpur, said the syllabus for all 41 diploma engineering courses has been revised to include a new AI unit. After being vetted by AKTU, the revised syllabus was sent to the Board of Technical Education, where the curriculum committee approved its implementation from the new academic session. He said a basic understanding of AI has become essential for students of every engineering discipline because of changing technological requirements. New units of IT and AI will be included The newly introduced unit has been titled Introduction to IT and AI. Besides introducing students to Artificial Intelligence, it will also cover cyber security and modern digital technologies. Experts said AI is no longer limited to computer science and information technology, but is increasingly being used in mechanical, electrical, civil, electronics and other engineering fields. Theory followed by practical training Students will study AI theory during the first and second semesters before moving on to practical sessions that teach them how to use AI tools. The syllabus includes topics such as Cyber Security Principles and Threats, Basic Protection Mechanisms, Cyber Security Practices, Fundamentals of AI, Prompt Engineering, Machine Learning and Deep Learning. During practical sessions, students will learn to use AI for preparing documents, creating videos and developing other forms of digital content.
