stories.title: 'Babua will remain a child all his life':Yogi takes jibe at Akhilesh; says 'Evening gatherings were routine, change requires hitting the ground'
stories.summary: On National Handloom Day, CM Yogi Adityanath said that those who held power in the state before 2017 had no vision for development. When people in power are not interested in work, the state's deterioration is inevitable. Due to this irresponsibility, the state remained engulfed in months of curfews and riots. Innocent children died from diseases like encephalitis and dengue. Without naming the SP chief, Yogi took a jibe, saying: Some people get associated with a word in life that they can never shake off. Some people remain children throughout their lives. Babua was also like that. He would wake up at 12 noon, get ready by 2 pm, go to the gym at 5 pm, and by 7 pm the gathering would be in full swing. Then how could he think about the state's development? Read the key points from CM Yogi's speech Vote bank politics worsened the situation before 2017 The Chief Minister said that before the BJP government was formed in the country in 2014 and in UP in 2017, work for the development of artisans could have been done, but it requires thinking and vision. He listed three shortcomings of the SP government- 1- Deterioration of education: Earlier, basic schools were in bad condition. There was neither arrangement for drinking water nor toilets. Today, schools are providing bags, uniforms, and modern facilities. PM Modi's 'Nipun Bharat Abhiyan' is being implemented on the ground. 2. Security and Infrastructure: Before 2017, the state had neither electricity, nor roads, nor law and order. Daughters and traders were not safe. When markets remain deserted, it affects every artisan, woman, and youth. 3. Plunder and Insecurity: Previous governments had no interest in development works; there was just a race for plunder within the dynasty, and they themselves posed a threat to women's safety. Handloom and Handicrafts received a new identity CM Yogi stated that the handloom and powerloom industry is UP's great heritage. About 30 lakh people's livelihoods are connected to it, of which 70% are women workers. Last year, the government provided electricity facilities worth ₹109 crores to 40 thousand artisans. Before 2017, Bhadohi's carpet cluster had become almost inactive. Today, exports worth crores of rupees are happening from there to world markets. Prime Minister Narendra Modi himself took the initiative and had Bhadohi carpets laid in the country's new Parliament building. When we appreciate the sweat of our artisans and encourage them, the country's money will remain in the country and prosperity will reach directly to the homes of craftspeople. 'Chief Minister and Ministers have to descend into the field' CM Yogi said in the end that the transformation of the state is possible when the Chief Minister himself takes out time to visit every district and ministers go to ground zero. In our government, every scheme is reaching directly to the public without any discrimination and vote bank politics.

stories.title: Car gutted in Lucknow, youth burnt alive:Only skeleton left by the time fire brigade arrived; one hand found stuck in seat
stories.summary: A young man was burnt to death in a Maruti Zen car that caught fire around 11:30 PM on Thursday night in Lucknow. He could not get out of the car after it caught fire. By the time the fire brigade brought the fire under control, only his skeleton remained inside the car. The accident occurred near Saraiya Mod in the Bakshi Ka Talab (BKT) area. According to the police, the cause of the car fire is not yet clear. It is also not known whether the car caught fire while moving or if it was stationary at the time. The body has been sent for post-mortem. Young man's body found burnt on the driving seat ACP Vikas Pandey said that at around 11:30 PM, information was received about a car catching fire on the highway. When the police and fire brigade reached the spot, the car was completely engulfed in flames. After extinguishing the fire, when the car door was opened, a completely burnt body of a person was found on the driving seat. Only a skeleton remained on the seat. The forensic team was called upon receiving the information, and they collected evidence from the scene. In the initial investigation, the body could not be identified. Police identified based on car number Based on the car's number, the police traced its owner. Investigation revealed that the car was registered in the name of Almash, son of Hamidul, a resident of Khurramnagar. Upon contacting the family, it was confirmed that the body found inside the car was that of 32-year-old Almash. The ACP stated that the family is being interrogated. The cause of the car fire has not yet been clarified. The matter is being investigated keeping all aspects in mind. Another body found inside a car in Ashiana Meanwhile, the body of a person was recovered from an abandoned Swift Dzire car at Salenagar intersection in Ashiana police station area around 11:57 PM on Thursday night. According to local residents, the car had been parked on the roadside for the past three days. When a strong foul smell emanated from it on Thursday night, people informed the police. Upon receiving the information, Ashiana police reached the spot, took possession of the car, and started an investigation. During the search, the body was found inside the car. According to the police, the car's registration number is UP 33 BB 8989. The body was identified as Gyanendra Singh, son of Uday Bhan Singh, a resident of Niralanagar, Raebareli.

stories.title: VIDEO | 2 groups of schoolgirls clash outside Gorakhpur school:Argument escalates to physical altercation, hair-pulling
stories.summary: On Wednesday evening, after school hours, a fierce fight broke out between two groups of girl students at the gate of an inter college located in Chargaon, Shahpur area of Gorakhpur. First, there was an argument, which quickly escalated into a physical altercation. Someone viralized a video of this street fight on social media. It is being reported that on Wednesday evening around 4 PM, after school hours, the girl students came out of the school. During this, an argument started between two students over some issue. According to eyewitnesses, as the dispute escalated, students from one side started verbally abusing and physically assaulting the other student. During the incident, a crowd of passersby and other students gathered outside the school gate. Attempts were made to intervene, but both sides continued to clash with each other. Principal said - Investigation underway The school principal stated that as soon as information about the incident was received, the matter was taken seriously. On Thursday, the students involved in the dispute did not come to school. The entire matter is being investigated. Action will be taken as per rules if found guilty. The police say that no complaint has been received from either side so far. An investigation is also being conducted based on the video. The school administration has appealed to students and parents to maintain discipline.

stories.title: Auto-rickshaw driver's body found in Varuna river:Son says, 'Cop had been following him for three days'; police probe underway
stories.summary: A commotion erupted after the body of an auto driver was found in the Varuna River near Varuna Bridge in the Cantt police station area of Varanasi. The Kachahri outpost in-charge had reached the spot with police force upon receiving information about an abandoned auto standing on Varuna Bridge. A bottle of acid was found inside the auto. Following this, when police started searching, a body was found floating in the Varuna River. The police then informed the family members using the auto's number, retrieved the body, and sent it to the mortuary. The deceased's son, who reached the spot, alleged that his father had said that some policeman had been following him for three days. Meanwhile, police have started investigating the case. The causes of the incident are being ascertained through CCTV footage. Police arrived upon receiving information about an abandoned auto People had informed the Cantt police station that an abandoned auto bearing number UP 65 ET 8037 was standing on Varuna Bridge, with a bottle of acid kept in the front. The Kachahri outpost in-charge immediately reached the spot and gathered information about the auto, which was found to be registered in the name of Rajendra Prasad Gupta. On this, the chowki in-charge called, and they informed that their auto is driven by Gyanchand Sonkar. His number was taken and his family members were called. Boy who reached the spot made allegations After receiving information, Gyanchand Sonkar's son Ashish Sonkar reached the spot. Police got the auto identified. After that, when searched, a body was found floating in the Varuna. His son Ashish identified it as Gyanchand. Ashish said that during Sawan, everyone had gone to Ayodhya but father had not gone. For the past three days, he was saying that some policeman was following him. And today his body has been found. Police engaged in investigation Cantt Thana in-charge Raj Kishore Pandey said - The body has been taken out of the water and sent to the mortuary. The post-mortem of the body will be conducted today. Further action will be taken based on the statement of the family members. Meanwhile, police are checking CCTV footage.

stories.title: Abaan Ahmed suffered ruptured liver and lungs, broken ribs:Died from 23 injuries, post-mortem reveals; brother broke down upon seeing body
stories.summary: 23 injuries were found on the body of Abaan (21), son of mafia Atiq Ahmed, in Jhansi. The post-mortem report revealed that his liver, lungs, and spleen ruptured due to a high-impact collision. His ribs were also broken. He died due to excessive internal bleeding. Meanwhile, Sonu, Abaan's companion who was sitting behind Aban's seat in the car, died due to a fractured skull. Fractures were found in both his arms. Both were post-mortemed by a panel of 3 doctors at Jhansi Medical College on Thursday night at 11:30 PM. Aban's elder brother, Ahjam, reached inside the post-mortem house. Seeing the body of his brother Aban, he burst into tears. Relatives consoled him. After this, he asked the police for the post-mortem report. Officials said they would provide the report later. After the post-mortem, Ahjam, along with relatives, placed both bodies in the same ambulance. They departed for Prayagraj with the bodies at 12 AM. Both will be cremated today. On Thursday, Abaan was going to meet his elder brother Ali Ahmed, who is imprisoned in Abaan Jhansi Jail. Four friends were with him in the Creta car. His car collided with the divider in the Poonch area, 70 km before Jhansi on the Jhansi-Kanpur Highway. Aban and Sonu died in the accident. His 3 friends Umar Ahmed, Mohammad Zaid and Farooq Ahjam were injured. Dr. Rajneesh, who conducted the post-mortem, said- Both died due to injuries sustained in the accident. First, Aban's body was post-mortemed. After this, Sonu's body was post-mortemed. Both were post-mortemed along with Dr. Pankaj Mustaria and Dr. Zia Zafar. See 2 pictures of the accident- So much internal bleeding occurred in Abaan's body that it came out of his mouth. Aban was sitting in the front seat of the car. His friend Zaid was driving the car. Sonu was sitting behind Abaan. The car, travelling at a speed of about 120 km/h, hit the divider on the side where Abaan was sitting. This is why Aban sustained the most injuries in the accident. Shortly after the collision, Abaan and Sonu died on the spot. Eyewitness Deepak Yadav, who was the first to arrive after the accident, said - I heard the noise and was the first to reach. I tried to open the car door, but it wouldn't open. After that, I brought a crowbar (iron rod) from a house and broke the door. Deepak said - After opening the door, I first pulled out a young man. His mouth was full of blood. He said - My name is Aban, save me. After this, he became unconscious. Aban had left Prayagraj for Jhansi at 5 AM on Thursday. The Creta car hit the divider in the Poonch police station area. The impact was so strong that the car was thrown about 7 feet into the air. Its pieces were scattered about 40 feet across the highway. The left side of the car was severely damaged. Brother said - Let the brothers be brought for burial Upon receiving news of Abaan's death in the accident, his elder brother Ahjam reached Jhansi from Prayagraj. First, he reached the accident site and gathered information from the police. After this, he went directly to Jhansi Medical College. Here, he met all three injured. Ahjam said - Let the brothers be brought for burial. After Ahjam arrived, the police completed the inquest for both bodies and conducted post-mortems. Ahjam has also given a written complaint to the police, based on which the police may register a case. Sonu's brother-in-law, who arrived in Jhansi from Satna to collect Sonu's body, said - Sonu used to work with trailers. He had come home from Dubai some time ago. stories.title: Rain lashes Lucknow, highway flooded in Farrukhabad:River swallows 50 acres in Lakhimpur; rainfall 150% above normal in 24 hours
stories.summary: The spell of monsoon rain continues across Uttar Pradesh. Lucknow received rain early on Friday, while around 40 cities, including Agra and Jaunpur, remained cloudy. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for all 75 districts today, with a heavy rainfall warning for 18 districts. According to the IMD, the state has received 19.3 mm of rainfall, which is 150% above the normal 7.8 mm. Heavy rain on Thursday evening inundated homes and schools in Bijnor. Waterlogging was reported on a national highway in Farrukhabad and in several residential areas. In Rae Bareli, a road caved in after the rain, leaving a three-foot-deep crater. Rivers are also in spate due to continuous rainfall. In Lakhimpur Kheri, the Sharda River has eroded around 50 acres of land so far. In Ballia, 27 houses have been washed away by the Saryu River. In Farrukhabad, the Ganga has risen close to the danger mark, with floodwater entering 33 villages and 40 government schools. The Ganga is also flowing above normal levels in Varanasi. Floodwater has entered 40–50 small temples, while the Ratneshwar Mahadev Temple is more than half submerged. A crocodile was spotted roaming on flooded roads in Lakhimpur Kheri. Forest department officials also rescued a Russell's viper that had entered a house and released it into the forest. Meanwhile, more than 20 cities, including Lucknow, Saharanpur and Meerut, received rainfall on Thursday morning. Due to continuous rain and rain-related incidents over the past three days, schools up to Class 8 have been closed. Rain-related accidents have also continued. In Barabanki, a dilapidated wall collapsed on five children on their way to a madrasa. All five were trapped under the debris. A 7-year-old boy and his 14-year-old sister died, while the other three children were rescued by villagers and taken to hospital. In Pratapgarh, a 100-year-old house collapsed amid continuous rain, killing 13 members of the same family. See pictures of floods and rain... Lucknow weather scientist Atul Kumar Singh said- The monsoon system has now become active over UP. It is passing through Delhi, Lucknow and Patna. Due to this, several cyclones have become active. Monsoon winds have reached the plains of the Ganges. Due to its effect, there will be heavy rainfall across the state for the next 4 to 5 days.

As Samajwadi Party legislators laughed at the party's small strength in the House, Singh responded without showing any anger. Calmly and politely, he said, "The party you are laughing at today. stories.title: Senior officials spared, juniors punished over Kanpur Expressway mess:Responsible officers cleared files blindly, without inspecting the site
stories.summary: The dilapidated condition of the country's most expensive Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway has ruined the image of the Union Ministry of Road Transport. The department and NHAI (National Highways Authority of India) are facing disrepute all around. NHAI had to blacklist the construction company of a BJP leader's brother. In a hurry, the Authority tried to show by taking action against some officers that it would not spare those responsible. But the truth is that there are others responsible on whom no action has been taken. Because when the expressway was being built for a long time, what were the officers sitting above doing? Did they check the quality or allow morang and asphalt to be laid based on estimates? Are those responsible for the shoddy construction being protected? In this report by Dainik Bhaskar, we will tell who else is responsible for this. First, let's tell which 3 officers NHAI held responsible and took action against them- Major culprits of the irregularity, against whom no action was taken Responsibility - NHAI's Regional Officer Gautam is based in Lucknow. His job is to monitor NHAI projects in UP and conduct quality checks through periodic site visits. Negligence - Initially, the first defect came to light on July 26. Then he tried to suppress the matter. He said there was a problem with bitumen (coal tar) in a small area. After the matter got out of hand, action was taken against the Project Manager and the Director. Dainik Bhaskar tried to contact Vishal Gautam. The call was answered, but immediately disconnected. When called again, the phone was not picked up. Responsibility - After Saurabh Chaurasia, Sharad became the Project Director of the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway and remained in this position for about 1 year. He was responsible for managing important technical arrangements during construction. Negligence - During his tenure, instead of inspecting the quality by visiting the site, he blindly trusted files and reports. Due to less visits to ground zero, he kept approving every file with 'OK', overlooking construction deficiencies. Dainik Bhaskar tried to contact him, but it was not possible. Responsibility - He is the head of PNC Infratech, the company building the expressway. The company is named after 3 brothers - Pradeep, Naveen, and Chakresh. Naveen Jain is a Rajya Sabha MP from BJP. Negligence - Secured a two-phase tender by bidding a total of ?2926 crore, but paid no attention to site monitoring and quality control during construction. No concrete information could be found about them either. Could not be contacted despite efforts. Now know about two cases of irregularities, in which the company owner was held responsible- What was the responsibility of the officials against whom action was taken? Responsibility- He was the highest-ranking officer for construction work in the field. It was his responsibility to get every layer of soil and gravel inspected and send the report upwards. Negligence- Ignored quality and committed irregularities in the field. Action- On July 30, NHAI removed him from the project and banned him for 2 years. Responsibility- He remained Project Director from the start of construction until 2024. The maximum construction happened during his tenure. Negligence- Instead of inspecting on-site, he blindly trusted PNC's reports. The foundation of irregularities was laid during his time. Action- NHAI has issued a charge sheet, framing the charges. Responsibility- Posted in the position for the last 1 year. The work was completed and inaugurated during his tenure. Negligence- 95% of the Greenfield area work was completed a year ago. Still, they gave an 'all okay' report without checking the quality. Action- Removed from NHAI and attached to PWD. 3 Crores Spent to Repair Sunken Expressway According to NHAI, 3 crores have been spent so far on the repair of the 63 km long expressway. This cost will be borne by PNC Infratech. The company has also been fined 2% of the performance security. The negligence of Theme Engineering Services Private Limited, which monitors the quality of construction, has come to light. Therefore, this company will be excluded from future projects. NHAI itself is getting the quality checked After the embarrassment, NHAI will now get the expressway inspected with a laser profilometer. This technique uses a laser beam to measure the texture, roughness, and height of an object's surface. It creates an accurate 3D map of the surface without touching it, which will precisely reveal the irregularities. How is a non-performer company building the Bahraich Expressway? NHAI admitted that earthwork, drainage, and quality were overlooked. Still, NHAI officials avoided taking action against the company. PNC has been awarded the work for the expressway from Barabanki to Bahraich. PNC has also been given the work of constructing a flyover inside Lucknow city. PNC Company's 'Tarnished' Record

stories.title: Atiq Ahmed's son writhed in car for 2 minutes:'My name is Abaan, save me'; eyewitness recounts final moments
stories.summary: "My name is Abaan... save me." Only this much could come out of his mouth. People pulled him out of the car, but within two minutes of struggling, his breathing stopped. These were the last words of mafia Atiq Ahmed's youngest son Aban Ahmed (21). Abaan was going to meet his brother Ali, who was imprisoned in Jhansi jail. He had also bought two romantic novels for his brother. When Ali received the news of the accident in jail, he started crying. Abaan was very dear to him. Perhaps this was the reason why Abaan had met Ali 49 times in 10 months. Dainik Bhaskar's team spoke with eyewitnesses, the injured, and police. Read the complete story of the last moments of the accident... First, let's understand how the accident happened? Abaan Ahmed left for Jhansi, 400 kilometers away from Prayagraj, around 5 AM on Thursday with his 2 friends and 2 relatives. But an accident occurred 70 kilometers before reaching there. Near Khilli village in Poonch, while trying to save a calf that suddenly appeared on the highway, the Creta car went out of control. It crashed into a concrete wall built on the roadside. At that time, the car was traveling at a speed of about 120. The collision was so severe that the car flew about 7 feet in the air and its pieces scattered up to 40 feet on the highway. In the accident, Abaan and his friend Sonu died on the spot, while three people were injured. Broke car doors with rods and pulled people out Eyewitness Sakesh said, ''I was working at my shop. Suddenly there was a loud explosion. It felt like something had burst. Several people present around the shop ran to the spot. Saw that there was a severe car collision. Immediately called 112 and got an ambulance. Until the ambulance and police arrived, we ourselves got engaged in rescuing the injured and trapped people. The car doors were jammed. Before the police arrived, we broke the doors with iron rods and pulled out the injured. Later, the police and ambulance took them to the hospital.'' Accident while trying to save a calf, car crashed into wall Eyewitness Deepak Yadav said - I was going from home to the field. Then I saw that a calf was crossing the highway. To save it, the car driver turned the vehicle to the left. Meanwhile, a biker came, and to save him, the car driver turned the car even more to the left. The very next moment, the car crashed into a wall built on the roadside. Some people came running. The injured were pulled out of the car. One injured person's mouth was filled with blood. When we asked his name, he said, "My name is Abaan. Save me." After this, he didn't say anything. His breathing stopped. 10 minutes after calling, the police arrived at the spot. The police took all the injured to the hospital in an ambulance. One part of the car was damaged; Aban-Sonu were sitting on this side According to the police, 5 people were sitting in the car. Mohammad Zaid (35) was driving the vehicle, and Abaan Ahmad (21) was sitting next to him. Sonu (24) was on the seat behind Abaan. Next to Sonu were Umar Ahmad (18) and Farooq Ahjam (28). The car was running close to the middle divider. The car crashed into a concrete wall built on the roadside towards the village. The front part was completely shattered. All airbags deployed. The left side of the car was more damaged. Abaan was sitting in the front on this side, and Sonu was sitting in the back. Both sitting on the left side died on the spot. Aban suffered serious head injuries. His hands and legs were broken. Aban-Sonu kept writhing in pain for 2 to 5 mins Eyewitness Ramakant said - Abaan and Sonu kept struggling for about two to five minutes, then their breathing stopped. Ambulance driver Pravesh said - All the injured were brought to CHC Moth. From there, I brought one injured person, Umar, to Jhansi Medical College. He had a fracture in his hand. The condition of all three injured was normal; they were talking. Village head Brijesh Kumar said - The car hit the divider due to loss of balance. The car's speed was high. After the accident, about 50 villagers and I reached the spot. Injured Mohammad Umar said - Car hit the divider Mohammad Umar, injured in the accident, said - The car was at high speed. Suddenly, after losing control, it crashed into the divider. The collision was so severe that Abaan and his friend Sonu died on the spot. Umar was not informed about brother Abaan's death Lucknow Jail's Jailer Ritwik Priyadarshi said - Atiq's elder son Umar has not been informed about Abaan's death. Information is given only as per the protocol prescribed in the jail. Family members have contacted lawyers of Prayagraj District Court to allow Atiq Ahmed's two sons imprisoned in jail to participate in Abaan's funeral. The lawyers replied that a parole application will have to be filed in the High Court. Two books and cigarette pack found in the car The Creta car (UP70 FW2432) belongs to Zaid; it was received as a wedding gift. Zaid is the son-in-law of Atiq's khaleri, that is, his maternal cousin sister. Two books were found in the car - 'The Stationery Shop of Tehran' and 'The Idiot'. Besides this, a cigarette pack was also found. Was going to meet Ali in jail with friends and relatives See pictures related to the accident- Brother left with the body late at night after post-mortem Abaan's body was kept in the post-mortem house of Jhansi Medical College. After the post-mortem, the body was handed over to brother Ahjam. Abaan will be buried next to Atiq's grave in Prayagraj on Friday.

stories.title: Brij Bhushan says, 'Priyanka was misled into turning against him':'It was only a good touch-bad touch allegation'; vows to return to Parliament
stories.summary: Former BJP MP from Uttar Pradesh Brij Bhushan Singh staged a show of strength on Thursday and spoke to Dainik Bhaskar about the women wrestlers' sexual harassment allegations, the alleged conspiracy, and politics. He said, "They turned a matter of good touch and bad touch into a movement. Posters appeared in Canada and the US. Some people were working behind the scenes. Bhupinder Singh Hooda and Deepender Singh Hooda misled Priyanka Gandhi, who then joined the movement." Referring to his political future, he added, "Everything is fine now. The Parliament I was once not allowed to enter, I will return to that very Parliament." Read the full interview... After a long legal battle, court acquitted you; what would you say? Brij Bhushan: This entire matter was about 'good touch-bad touch'. I garlanded some players and gave medals to others, and I touched or hugged them after they won a wrestling match. Later, it was said that they were uncomfortable during that time. But this was turned into such a big movement, as if something very serious had happened. There were poster wars and candle marches against me even in Canada and America. Priyanka Gandhi, farmer leaders, and even Khalistanis sitting in Canada got involved in this. It was given a caste and regional color. You are continuously talking about conspiracy; according to you, who were the people behind it? Brij Bhushan: In this conspiracy, some faces were visible in front, and some were behind the curtain. If I have to name them, the most prominent role was played by Bhupinder Singh Hooda and Deepender Singh Hooda. They also misled senior Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi and connected her to this movement. Apart from this, many big lawyers, big capitalists, and a large part of the opposition were involved in it. Politics and wrestling- was there an attempt to snatch both in this conspiracy? Brijbhushan: You can say that, but an even more serious attempt was to destroy my character. Character assassination of any person is the biggest sin. The athletes who made the allegations were on the world and Olympic level, so the wrong message went out to the entire world. But after the court's decision, the truth is now in front of everyone. Will you now make an active comeback in both politics and wrestling? Brijbhushan. Where did I go? Neither from politics nor from society. I had said earlier that I will definitely return one day to the Parliament where attempts were made to stop me from entering. I am fully confident that my return to Parliament is certain. What do you think is the reason for the way people came out in your support in Ayodhya? Brijbhushan: This is not support of one day. This is the result of my nearly 50 years of penance. Since the age of 17-18, I have been working among people for public issues. The crowd that was seen on the roads today is the result of that long social and political relationship. Saints on your platform raised the issue of misuse of laws related to women; what would you say? Brij Bhushan: Laws are extremely necessary for the safety and security of women and daughters, but if they are being misused, then there should be serious discussion on it. Saints have raised this issue; if public support is built in society, then further discussion will happen. For now, there is no plan for any movement. What is your view on opposition parties and movements happening in the country? Brij Bhushan: The job of the opposition is to raise public issues. But an old party like Congress has not conducted any major movement under its own banner in the last 10 years. They only mislead people by joining others' movements, whether it's the farmers' movement, the wrestlers' issue, or recent movements.

stories.title: How a Massachusetts cranberry farm became a thriving wetland
stories.summary: A former cranberry farm in Plymouth, Massachusetts, has been transformed into a thriving freshwater wetland after restoration work began in 2010. The project restored 225 acres of wetland and more than three miles of stream habitat, removed dams and barriers, and brought back native plants and wildlife. Thousands of migratory fish, including alewife and blueback herring, returned to areas they had been unable to reach for more than 100 years.

The island was once a city dump where methane gas caused underground fires. The soil helped cap the old landfill, reshape the island and support a long restoration effort that brought back trees, plants, birds and other wildlife.

Local communities are banding together to protect and celebrate this unparalleled cultural legacy, ensuring that the spirit of the Ama continues to thrive amidst adversity.

stories.title: Mercury is still shrinking as its cooling core cracks the planet's thin crust
stories.summary: Mercury's massive metallic core leads to a contraction of its rocky exterior, resulting in numerous fractures and cliffs spanning hundreds of kilometers. Researchers examine these formations to gain insight into Mercury's internal mechanics, with future missions expected to deliver clearer images of these relatively young tectonic anomalies.

This achievement underscores the significance of indigenous-led land management and collaborative approaches to preserving natural habitats.

stories.title: ED director Rahul Navin's tenure extended by a year

stories.title: 7 of 25 high courts without CJs, collegium recommends names for just four
stories.summary: The Supreme Court collegium recommended four judges for High Court Chief Justice positions. These appointments aim to fill vacancies in key High Courts across India. The collegium also approved transfers of two judges from Orissa High Court. Orissa High Court faces a significant shortage of judges, impacting its functioning. No representation from Orissa High Court has been appointed to the Supreme Court in eight years.

stories.title: Recent rain has little impact on national monsoon deficit
stories.summary: Recent rains have brought relief to Delhi, Haryana, and eastern Rajasthan, yet the national monsoon deficit persists. States like Bihar and Punjab continue to struggle with below-average rainfall. While the sowing of Kharif crops is nearly finalized across the nation, August's rainfall may enhance water reservoirs for hydropower and upcoming planting seasons, with a low-pressure area potentially raising precipitation levels in eastern India shortly.

stories.title: Claim On Leaving Kick Misleads: Fact-check says exit not confirmed; streamer plans multistreaming
stories.summary: Clavicular’s multistreaming announcement is real, but claims that he has completely left Kick are not confirmed. Braden Peters said he plans to multistream and named Twitch and X as the most likely platforms. He did not say he would stream exclusively there. His Kick channel remains active, so the stronger claim goes beyond what he actually announced.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Arthur Schopenhauer: 'Talent hits a target no one else can hit. Genius hits...'
stories.summary: Arthur Schopenhauer articulated a clear distinction between talent and genius, describing talent as the ability to achieve well-defined goals while genius encompasses a visionary perspective, identifying targets that remain hidden to most. This insight delineates how talent thrives within established frameworks, whereas genius disrupts norms, prompting transformative change. This philosophical distinction is essential for fostering creativity and personal growth in contemporary contexts.

stories.title: Austin McBroom Spider-Man controversy takes new turn as woman accused of sexual assault shares her side
stories.summary: The woman featured in Austin McBroom's infamous Spider-Man livestream has now shared her story, revealing that she was compensated to take part in the orchestrated skit. Her announcement comes amid a surge of discussions online regarding the reality of the incident. Accompanying her claims were messages that confirmed both the premeditated nature of the scene and her payment, shedding light on the ongoing debate.

stories.title: Search ops involving Indian Navy for 3 missing fishermen continue in Kerala: Official
stories.summary: The Indian Navy's search for three missing fishermen continues into its tenth day. Divers are utilizing portable SONAR to enhance underwater surveillance capabilities. INS Kalpeni joined the operation, sailing from Kochi to aid the search efforts. The search initially focused on Gautam Krishna, who went missing off the Neendakara coast. The operation is ongoing off the Kollam and Thiruvananthapuram coasts.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Zhuangzi: 'Rewards and punishment is the lowest form of education'
stories.summary: The ancient philosopher Zhuangzi posited that rewards and punishments represent the most rudimentary form of education. He argued that relying on external controls stifles true human nature and impedes natural growth. Today, many educational systems still employ grades and fear tactics, manipulating students similarly to animals. Supporting this, Edward Deci's studies indicate that external rewards can diminish intrinsic enjoyment.

stories.title: Asmongold reveals health scare while breaking silence on latest Twitch ban and 2-week suspension
stories.summary: Asmongold, the popular streamer, faced a worrying health incident reminiscent of his father's condition, prompting a visit to the emergency room where doctors reassured him that he was fine. Meanwhile, his Twitch channel is under a two-week suspension starting from August seventh, believed to stem from remarks about migrants, which he plans to appeal. Asmongold intends to use this period for important health assessments and to navigate his channel's suspension.

stories.title: Police search 26 locations tied to banned Jamaat-e-Islami J&K
stories.summary: Authorities conducted extensive searches at twenty-six locations in Sopore, north Kashmir, specifically targeting the premises of Jamaat-e-Islami J&K. Critical documents and electronic devices were seized amid an investigation into the organization’s potential ties to terrorism. This operation is part of an intensified effort in the area following the tragic shooting of a police officer, highlighting ongoing security threats posed by the banned group.

stories.title: No more strikes on Iran? Trump says US going 'low key', stresses economic pressure over military op
'Ranchi police fully prepared': Jharkhand braces for students' protest march to Assembly
Denmark shooting: Several wounded as police suspect gang-related feud
stories.summary: A shooting incident in Holbaek on Sunday left several individuals injured. Local police were alerted to the situation around 3:45 PM, promptly responding to the chaotic scene. Authorities are investigating the possibility that this attack is linked to ongoing rivalries among criminal groups. Reports suggest that the suspects fled the area in a white vehicle. Police are asking for any witnesses or information to aid in the investigation.

stories.title: In 1987, Orlando put 1,200 acres of constructed wetlands to work cleaning reclaimed water
stories.summary: Orlando's constructed wetlands, established in 1987, treat billions of gallons of reclaimed water annually. Aquatic plants absorb nutrients, but decaying matter creates sediment buildup over time. Periodic earthmoving, known as demucking, removes this organic muck to restore marsh function. This process involves draining, scraping, and replanting native species in 100-acre sections. Such long-term maintenance ensures the wetland's continued effectiveness in water purification.

stories.title: Florida community fears radioactive waste pile could threaten many living nearby
stories.summary: Residents of Progress Village are increasingly concerned about the environmental and health threats posed by a substantial phosphogypsum stack nearby. This waste contains naturally occurring radioactive materials, raising alarms about radiation exposure and potential water contamination, particularly during storm events. Studies on the stack's effects on local air and water quality have been conducted, and the community is advocating for greater transparency and improved management of this hazardous industrial waste.

stories.title: 'Reflection of public anger': Suvendu Adhikari after Mamata Banerjee faces protests, called 'chor'
7 civilians killed in Russia-Ukraine overnight strikes; Moldova reports drone explosion
stories.summary: The ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine escalated overnight, with strikes claiming the lives of seven civilians and injuring many others. Russian drones and missiles targeted Kharkiv and Odesa, causing severe damage. In retaliation, Ukraine's drone strikes in Russia's Belgorod region killed five individuals. Furthermore, a powerful explosion near Moldova's border hinted at the presence of combat drones. Hostilities continue as both nations prioritize attacks on military and infrastructural objectives.

stories.title: In 1986, a California city began polishing sewage through constructed marshes
stories.summary: Arcata's groundbreaking wastewater treatment approach utilizes beautifully designed constructed wetlands, turning once barren industrial land into a vibrant wildlife haven. This innovative system now attracts over 300 bird species migrating along the Pacific Flyway, providing not only a unique habitat but also recreational opportunities and educational experiences for the public. This remarkable civic initiative has garnered national acclaim for its commitment to sustainability.

stories.title: ED director Rahul Navin gets 1-year extension
In the 1990s, New York chose wetlands over conventional storm sewers on Staten Island
stories.summary: In an innovative move, New York City has turned to its natural wetlands for stormwater management, resulting in significant cost savings. The Bluebelt initiative has replaced expensive underground drainage systems with revitalized waterways, integrating both green and grey infrastructure to manage runoff efficiently. This strategic framework not only safeguards and extends essential wetland areas but also boosts the city's resilience against the impacts of climate change and pollution.

stories.title: Trump's hair-do turns heads, has America all tangled up
DGCA to conduct preliminary probe into Baramati aircraft runway excursion: Centre
'Attempt to murder': TMC MPs blame BJP for attack on Mamata Banerjee's car, claim CM Suvendu link
stories.summary: Trinamool Congress leaders accused the BJP of orchestrating an attack on Mamata Banerjee's vehicle. Stones and objects were reportedly hurled at her car while she traveled to meet a grieving family. TMC MPs described the incident as an attempt to murder and a failure of governance. Mamata Banerjee herself stated the attack could have caused serious injuries or death.

stories.title: Florida drained land for a giant subdivision in the 1960s; 2026 restoration reverses it
stories.summary: The Picayune Strand Restoration Project in Southwest Florida has been completed after years of work to restore the natural flow of water across 55,000 acres of wetlands. The project removed more than 260 miles of roads and plugged almost 50 miles of canals. The work is expected to improve wetlands, water quality and wildlife habitat.

stories.title: Trump ready to end Iran war without nuclear deal; Tehran's demands complicate exit: Report
In 2001, Denmark began turning 19 km of straightened River Skjern into 26 km of bends
stories.summary: Denmark's River Skjern is undergoing a restoration project aimed at reversing the environmental impact caused by historical drainage efforts. The river now floods more of its floodplain, but artificial channels hinder its natural dynamics. While some aquatic species are bouncing back, the diversity from its past remains largely absent. The limited recreation of key backwater habitats suggests that further proactive restoration measures may be necessary for a truly ecological revival.

stories.title: Punjab: AAP's youth wing holds marathon in Mohali
People of 'Devbhoomi' always stand firm on national duty, says CM Dhami; commends 'Tiranga Yatra' response
Evening news wrap: Air India turbulence-hit flight captain’s dope test returns 'not negative'; Israel rejects US Gaza proposal & more
stories.summary: An Air India captain's dope test returned non-negative after a turbulence-hit flight. Israel rejected the US Gaza peace proposal, demanding Hamas disarm first. Mamata Banerjee alleged her convoy faced stone-pelting during a visit to a deceased worker's family. Russia proposed a direct rail link to India to bypass maritime chokepoints. Pakistan's PML-N softened its stance on PoK protesters, calling most patriotic.

stories.title: Supreme Leader Khamenei footage to be released 'in future', Iran says as reports claim he is close to 'dead'
In 2010, Shanghai turned a polluted industrial brownfield into Houtan Park
stories.summary: Shanghai’s Houtan Park showcases the remarkable transformation of a contaminated industrial site into a thriving wetland that effectively purifies river water daily. The design cleverly integrates recycled materials, honoring local heritage while addressing waste reduction. Its ecological contributions include carbon sequestration and supporting wildlife recovery, setting a benchmark for urban flooding solutions and enriching communal spaces with nature.

stories.title: Jharkhand govt to scrap JPSC exams, rejects CGL cancellation demand; students vow to intensify stir
In 2023, Hoboken opened a 5.4-acre park on a former industrial site; its playgrounds can...
stories.summary: ResilienCity Park has officially opened in Hoboken, transforming a former industrial zone into a vital green space. This innovative park not only offers recreational facilities but also enhances the city's defense against severe flooding. Employing both above and below-ground stormwater storage, it showcases efficient flood-control methods. Supported by federal, state, and county funding, the initiative ensures residents won’t face tax hikes, setting a precedent for cities grappling with climate-related challenges.

stories.title: The women who paint Jharkhand: Sohrai-Khovar's journey from ritual to global gallery
ICE arrests over 1,200 illegal immigrants in Georgia
Ohio Uranium plant shut in 1989; $4.4 bn cleanup transformed site into green preserve
stories.summary: The Fernald uranium plant in Ohio stopped production in 1989 after nearly four decades of operations. A $4.4 billion environmental cleanup followed, involving radioactive waste, contaminated soil and groundwater. The 1,050-acre site was eventually transformed into the Fernald Preserve, with restored wetlands, prairie and forest. A Visitors Center now documents the site’s history and cleanup.

stories.title: Turbulence-hit AI flight captain screening dope test 'not negative, sent for confirmatory test:' Govt
India, Russia to be linked by rail? Moscow floats proposal, calls it 'viable'
‘We know how to stand up to American ideas': Israeli PM Netanyahu rejects Trump's 15-point Gaza plan
stories.summary: Israel has turned down a US proposal regarding the peace process in Gaza, with Prime Minister Netanyahu firmly asserting that Hamas must be completely disarmed before any Israeli forces withdraw. He mentioned that discussions are ongoing with Washington. Conversely, Hamas demands a complete Israeli troop withdrawal as a prerequisite for negotiation, reflecting significant barriers to advancing beyond the current ceasefire.

stories.title: 'Avoid comments that appease BJP': KC Venugopal to Cong leaders after Tharoor's CJP remarks
Redonda's wildlife roars back after rats and goats are removed
From 'enemies' to 'patriotic brothers': Pakistan changes stance on PoK protesters ahead of polls
US satellites hunting secret nuclear tests accidentally detected first gamma-ray burst in 1967
stories.summary: Gamma-ray bursts are among the most powerful explosions observed in the universe. First accidentally detected by Vela satellites in 1967, they puzzled scientists for decades. Research later showed that these bursts come from distant cosmic events, including massive stars collapsing and neutron star mergers. Yet their powerful jets still hold mysteries.

stories.title: This insect makes a house of silk and leaves and then carries it everywhere on its back
stories.summary: Bagworm caterpillars have an unusual way of protecting themselves. They build portable cases using silk produced by their own bodies and materials such as leaves, twigs and plant debris. The caterpillar carries this case wherever it moves, using it as both shelter and camouflage. The case grows as the caterpillar grows, with more material added to its outer surface. Some cases are made with tiny sticks and can resemble miniature log cabins, helping the insect blend into its surroundings.

stories.title: ‘Dialogue, not batons’: Jharkhand CM Soren's message to youth protesting for 'justice' over exam leaks
stories.summary: Jharkhand's Chief Minister Hemant Soren addressed the ongoing protests, urging young demonstrators to reject political affiliations. His commitment to transparency and justice regarding recruitment exam irregularities was clear as he highlighted the importance of discussions over confrontation. Soren warns that misinformation from rival factions aims to stir unrest, while the protests now stretch into their sixteenth day, keeping conversations alive.

stories.title: 'Anti-people': Congress vows to oppose FCRA Bill, Venugopal accuses Centre of targeting NGOs
stories.summary: Opposition parties plan to strongly protest the proposed Foreign Contribution Regulation Amendment Bill. This legislation is expected to be introduced in Parliament during the Monsoon Session. Congress leaders allege the bill targets minorities and NGOs, deeming it unconstitutional. They also raise concerns about student protest handling and delimitation proposals. Opposition parties are preparing for parliamentary debates and potential legislative actions.

stories.title: What happens after you apply for an organ transplant?
stories.summary: From medical evaluation and registry enrolment to waitlist priority, organ matching, surgery and lifelong follow-up, the transplant process in India involves multiple clinical, regulatory and coordination stages before a patient receives an organ.

stories.title: Gene gun makes lettuce and tobacco produce myoglobin for meat-like colour and flavour
How USS Colorado kept fighting after Japan hit it 22 times off Tinian during World War II
stories.summary: On July 24, 1944, hidden Japanese shore guns struck USS Colorado 22 times during the invasion of Tinian, killing 43 crew members and wounding 198. Despite the damage, the battleship continued firing and helped support the landings. Tinian was later captured and became a major U.S. bomber base in the Pacific.

stories.title: Indian man accused of strangling US girlfriend after she planned to end relationship; arrested in Germany
‘Stones, shoes thrown at my car’: Mamata faces protest during visit to kin of dead TMC worker
Three incidents that shaped Kailash Satyarthi’s life and work
'You'll have to answer for this crime': Rahul slams PM Modi, HM Shah over police action on students
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi criticized Prime Minister Modi and home minister Shah for their response to student protests. He stated that students are the nation's light and he stands with them. Gandhi highlighted student struggles with education and lack of employment opportunities. He warned youth against social media distractions as jobs are shrinking. The Congress leader alleged RSS ideology appointments affected institutional systems.

stories.title: ‘Situation difficult’: Zelensky in Moscow ally Serbia as Russian strikes kill 4 in Ukraine
Sharks fitted with sensors could help scientists improve hurricane forecasts
stories.summary: Sharks are being used as mobile ocean sensors by University of Delaware researchers in a new study that could help improve hurricane forecasts. Electronic tags attached to sharks collect water temperature, salinity and depth data as the animals move through the Atlantic. Scientists hope the information will improve understanding of ocean conditions that influence hurricane intensity.

stories.title: 'Shivling exists beneath its premises': Hindu outfit plans Ganga water offering at Deoband seminary
AI can help bridge India's healthcare gap: Report
PM must come to House and reply on Ram Mandir donation theft case: Mallikarjun Kharge
Budapest’s low Danube exposes two German soldiers and a DKW motorcycle buried for 80 years
stories.summary: Unusually low water levels in Budapest’s Danube River have exposed Second World War remains hidden for around 80 years. Recovery teams found the bodies of two Wehrmacht soldiers, their well-preserved identity discs, a German military motorbike, anti-tank mines and other wartime objects near Batthyány Square. The finds could help identify the soldiers and reveal more about Budapest’s final wartime days.

stories.title: How 10 billion trees transformed South Korea's post-war forests
NIA arrests main conspirator in Kerala illegal explosives seizure case; tenth arrest so far
Biologists tagged an 87-pound paddlefish in 2007; 18 years later, the fish weighed 98 pounds
stories.summary: An impressive paddlefish, initially tagged in 2007, made headlines when an angler recaught it after an astonishing eighteen years. This ancient species revealed invaluable long-term growth data to scientists, adding eleven pounds and increasing its length by three inches. Such recaptures are pivotal, offering critical insights into fish survival and migration, underscoring the necessity of sustained fish tagging initiatives for conservation efforts.

stories.title: Meta must comply with Indian law, not merely global policies: Centre
Houthi attack suspected at Saudi gas facility in Jubail; Aramco Jazan fire extinguished
'Internal matter': Supriya Sule on Sunetra Pawar-led NCP faction's talks with Prashant Kishor
Heavy rain likely across several states this week; Delhi surpasses August rainfall average
Tiranga Yatra: Patriotic marches held across UP, Haryana ahead of Independence Day
Scientists bred 39 surviving clams in Florida’s Indian River Lagoon; they have since outplanted 65 million
stories.summary: Florida's Indian River Lagoon shows signs of recovery after decades of environmental decline. Scientists are restoring critical habitats like reefs, shellfish beds, seagrass, and wetlands. Efforts focus on reintroducing clams, which were nearly extinct due to overharvesting and algal blooms. Millions of juvenile and adult "super clams" have been released into the lagoon. Local governments are addressing runoff issues to support the lagoon's ongoing restoration.

stories.title: Jharkhand student protest: Govt to hold fresh talks as fasting student leader's health worsens
Palau removed invasive rats; a year later, fish biomass rose 183% and leaf nitrogen jumped 80%
stories.summary: A new study from Ulong Island in Palau has found the first experimental evidence that restoring seabird populations by removing invasive rats can also help nearby coral reefs recover. Within a year, researchers recorded more seabirds, increased nutrient movement from land to sea and higher fish biomass, showing that island restoration can benefit both terrestrial and marine ecosystems.

stories.title: Britain is dropping 20 concrete reef cubes and 44 tons of scallop shells into the sea to bring back native oysters
stories.summary: Engineered concrete cubes are being deployed in Britain's North Sea to restore native oyster populations. These structures provide a stable foundation for oysters and habitat for marine life. The project aims to rebuild a collapsed ecosystem after a significant decline in oyster numbers. Volunteers are actively involved in cleaning and attaching oysters to the reef cubes.

stories.title: Amit Shah presents President's Colour to Puducherry Police
Pentagon asks defence firms to ramp up weapons production as Iran war drains stockpile: Report
Strait of Hormuz standoff: What Iran, US want and what it takes to reopen waterway
Colombia rocked by car bomb blast a day after new President takes charge
stories.summary: In southwestern Colombia, a car bomb detonated at a toll plaza on Saturday, just a day after Abelardo de la Espriella took office as president. The army promptly attributed the incident to dissident FARC factions, leaving two security guards injured. In response, President de la Espriella issued a stern warning to armed groups, urging them to comply with the rule of law.

stories.title: Four killed after helicopter crashes on steep hillside in Rio de Janeiro
Dozens of Nigerians freed after six months in jihadi captivity
Gen Z is a force that can’t be ignored: Dharmendra Pradhan
stories.summary: Former Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan acknowledged the immense potential of Gen Z, stating that grasping their hopes and dreams is essential for national advancement. He noted that the eagerness of young people surpasses any governmental duties, a point he shared with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who subsequently reached out to the youth. Pradhan maintained that prioritizing the nation's welfare is of utmost importance.

stories.title: EPFO, officers' body contest claims about new IT system
stories.summary: The rollout of EPFO's new IT system has resulted in a substantial backlog of claim issues. Field officials are grappling with an increasing number of pending auto claims, which have lingered for over twenty days and are causing significant discomfort to members. EPFO admits that this surge in pendency is a short-term effect of the system transition, although it was executed with minimal disruption to services.

stories.title: Captain moves crew to citadel, thwarts pirate assault on India-bound vessel
stories.summary: In a daring move, the Indian Navy successfully thwarted a pirate assault on the Golden Arsenal in the perilous Gulf of Aden. The ship’s crew effectively sought refuge within an impregnable citadel that the invaders could not penetrate. Currently, four vessels remain under the control of Somali pirates, with Indian nationals on three of them.

stories.title: US Vice President JD Vance calls PM Modi to discuss boosting ties
stories.summary: On Saturday, VP JD Vance engaged in a conversation with PM Narendra Modi, reiterating both nations' dedication to strengthen partnerships in vital sectors such as trade, defense, and upcoming technologies. They shared insights on international matters of shared concern, coinciding with the US Senate's approval of a bill focused on Russian oil transactions.

stories.title: Government appoints 30 judges to high courts of Calcutta, MP, Karnataka, Madras
stories.summary: The law ministry notified thirty new judges for four high courts on Saturday. Madras High Court received fifteen appointments, while Calcutta got eight and Karnataka six. Judicial officers and advocates were elevated to the benches, with most appointed as additional judges. Over sixty lakh cases are pending across India's twenty-five high courts. The law minister cited collegium delays for the significant number of vacancies.

stories.title: Captain of turbulence-hit Phuket-Delhi flight may have failed dope test
stories.summary: During a turbulent flight from Phuket to Delhi, the captain of an Air India aircraft reportedly tested positive for psychoactive substances. The turbulence caused a significant scare, resulting in hospitalization for thirteen passengers and four crew members. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation is conducting a detailed investigation, and the flight crew has been suspended from flying duties as per standard procedures.

stories.title: Proposed MDR for UPI transactions will be nominal, says government
stories.summary: The government has pledged that the upcoming UPI merchant discount rate will be minimal. This fee will be applicable only to certain merchants and transactions that surpass a designated threshold. Importantly, person-to-person UPI payments will remain free for all users. This initiative is designed to enhance the sustainability of India’s digital payment ecosystem and facilitate service expansion into rural and semi-urban regions.

stories.title: Government spending on education below Unesco's 15% standard
stories.summary: India's education funding aligns with GDP standards but falls short of public spending goals. Completion rates for secondary schools lag behind national and UNESCO guidelines. This funding pattern emerges as countries shift focus from education financial targets. India's extensive education initiatives benefit millions of students, yet the sector continues to grapple with persistent challenges despite increased program deployment.

stories.title: Rijiju, Rahul trade barbs over women's quota bill rollout
stories.summary: Union minister Kiren Rijiju called on LoP Rahul Gandhi to back the women's reservation bill during their exchange. In response, Rahul Gandhi noted that the 2023 bill had already received unanimous approval. He raised concerns about the holdup in implementing the legislation and its connection to the delimitation process. Gandhi insisted on prompt action to enforce the 2023 law, underscoring the heated political discourse on women's empowerment.

stories.title: 6 years after NDA exit, Punjab's SAD backs delimitation push
stories.summary: Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal now supports the women's reservation law rollout. This move signals the government's potential revival of the Constitution amendment bill. The government is also seeking support from DMK and NCP(SP) for the measure. The bill aims to increase Lok Sabha's strength by fifty percent. Its timing remains uncertain as lawmakers consider summoning Parliament.

stories.title: Kash Patel plans Russia trip in October; Kremlin-friendly newspaper warns he better not come empty-handed if he has a favor to ask
Two memorials of 1962 war heroes figure in 27 places formally named in Arunachal
stories.summary: The Union government has formally named twenty-seven locations in Arunachal Pradesh. These places include memorials honoring Indian Army war heroes from past conflicts. Havildar Shere Thapa and Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat are among those recognized for bravery. Several strategically important mountain passes and a logistics hub were also officially identified. This action pays homage to soldiers who sacrificed their lives defending India's borders.

stories.title: Quote of the day on love: 'Find what you love and let it kill you'
Flight to Toronto canceled as child refuses seatbelt, stands on seat; passengers stranded for 24 hours: 'Parents should be fined'
Restore J&K statehood, says human rights forum
stories.summary: An advocacy group for human rights calls for the restoration of statehood and the repeal of the 2019 Reorganisation Act. They argue that statehood should not be contingent upon the regional security situation. The forum additionally demands statehood for Ladakh and its inclusion in the Sixth Schedule. Their report highlights police inadequacies despite court mandates on detentions and brings attention to the injustices faced by Kashmiris after acts of terrorism.

stories.title: Raids in four Kashmir districts in anti-national narrative case
stories.summary: On Saturday, Counter Intelligence Kashmir executed raids at five locations spread across the districts of Baramulla, Bandipora, Anantnag, and Shopian. During these operations, several electronic and digital storage devices were confiscated as part of an investigation into an anti-national narrative. As of now, no arrests have been reported in relation to this ongoing case.

stories.title: Kashmir route outpaces Manali as Ladakh tourism surges
stories.summary: In the period from January to July, Ladakh has welcomed a remarkable 330,332 tourists. Air travel continues to be the favored mode of access to this stunning union territory. Among road travelers, the route through Kashmir is increasingly popular over the Manali path. Enhanced infrastructure and well-planned events have fueled this tourism surge, with burgeoning homestays offering fresh job opportunities for the local community.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Marco Polo: 'I did not write half of what I saw, for I knew I would not be believed', and how reality could be much larger than human imagination
FIR against 17 for assaulting 4 transporting bovines in J&K
stories.summary: Seventeen alleged cow vigilantes are facing legal action in Ramban after assaulting four men who were transporting bovines acquired from a police auction. The brutal incident, which occurred on August 4, resulted in one man suffering life-threatening injuries. This alarming event follows a fatal encounter in April, highlighting ongoing violence linked to cow protection. Investigations into wrongful restraint and assault are currently underway.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Neymar: "Messi is a great player. Playing against him is not good, it is…"
Death of PhD student Vikram Mubayi after California hike leaves family seeking answers
PM Modi speaks to US VP Vance, discusses ways to deepen India-US strategic partnership
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with US Vice President JD Vance on Saturday. They discussed deepening the India-US Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership across key areas. PM Modi also congratulated JD Vance and his wife Usha Vance. The Prime Minister conveyed his best wishes to the growing family. This conversation focused on strengthening bilateral relations between the two nations.

stories.title: A moth outbreak has killed off forests across Siberia, now the flammable wood is causing wildfires
stories.summary: In a catastrophic turn of events, a diminutive moth has decimated vast stretches of Siberian forest, transforming them into a fire hazard of monumental proportions. The Siberian silk moth's caterpillar stage ravages tree needles, resulting in widespread die-offs over several years. Major outbreaks have persisted over the decades, decimating millions of hectares, and now this ecological calamity aligns with an urgent wildfire emergency that has meteorological implications.

stories.title: Inside Portugal’s 19th-century goat tower, where dwarf goats climb a spiral ramp
Uttarakhand CM Dhami transfers Rs 146.32 crore pension benefits to 9.87 lakh beneficiaries
stories.summary: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Saturday transferred Rs 146.32 crore in pension benefits through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to 9,87,017 beneficiaries under various pension schemes of the Social Welfare Department for July 2026.

stories.title: ICE arrests at airports: Immigration lawyers share these 6 tips if you are stopped, questioned or detained
Major US university to hide grades for first-semester students, cites ‘mental health crisis’
Eggs thrown at Kosovo PM in parliament; House suspended amid political crisis
Meet Costa Rica's tiny 'coffee frog,' a nocturnal species found living among coffee shrubs
stories.summary: A remarkable discovery in Costa Rica reveals a diminutive nocturnal frog inhabiting the coffee plantations. Measuring less than four centimeters, this unique species relies on small insects for food and foliage for protection. Essential to its lifecycle are local streams, which face risks from pesticide runoff. This finding not only emphasizes the rich biodiversity in agricultural settings but also the urgent need for conservation initiatives.

stories.title: 'Should have gone to Ranchi': Rijiju takes dig at Rahul Gandhi over Prayagraj event
‘Gangstran Te Vaar’: Punjab Police acts against over 58,000 criminals in 200-day crackdown
2-year-old sister becomes perfect bone marrow match for Utah girl with aplastic anemia
stories.summary: Emma Meline, a young girl diagnosed with severe aplastic anemia right before Christmas, found hope in her little sister Lucy. At only two years old, Lucy bravely became a bone marrow donor, granting Emma the chance for a life-saving transplant. After a challenging journey, Emma celebrated her fifth birthday at home, marking a remarkable recovery. This profound experience deepened the unbreakable bond between the two sisters.

stories.title: Indian man on death row in the US for killing wife, in-laws in 2019 seeks retrial, says his previous lawyers were bad
'Dard, data, daulat': Rahul Gandhi targets Centre over unemployment at ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ event
Bihar should withdraw alcohol ban as it failed to curb crimes against women: Report
stories.summary: A research paper suggests Bihar should withdraw its alcohol prohibition policy. The ban has not reduced crimes against women, and illicit liquor trade has increased. Restoring liquor excise duty could boost state revenues by fifteen percent. The paper also identified education, health, and jobs as key development priorities. Bihar's development strategy should focus on these interconnected areas for progress.

stories.title: Safety vs privacy: How domestic-help platforms are building a two-way support system
stories.summary: The landscape of domestic help services in India is evolving as platforms aim to bolster user trust and safety. Emphasizing security, these services are implementing background checks and defining service hours. Furthermore, innovations such as AI technology and body cameras are continuously being assessed to improve safety measures. Moving forward, the success of the industry will depend on creating a trustworthy environment amidst its traditionally informal nature.

stories.title: Pests, mould, live insects: FSSAI suspends license of two food units
ICE rolls out body cameras, but policy lets agency decide which footage goes public
Dinosaur bone found in 1999 finally identified as 3-metre species after 27 years
Florida's millions of dumped tyres are still being cleaned up 50 years later
stories.summary: Florida is set to embark on an ambitious initiative to clear millions of old tires that were dumped offshore decades ago. Initially forming an artificial reef, these tires have since led to significant damage to natural coral ecosystems. Present surveys indicate that over half a million tires still litter thousands of acres.

stories.title: China dominates 80% of tungsten market; Nevada discovery faces NASA mining block
Jason Arday denies plagiarism claims; Cambridge reviews his appointment process
Supriya Sule opposes FCRA Bill, urges Centre to withdraw it or send it to JPC
stories.summary: Supriya Sule opposes the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, in its current form. She urges the government to withdraw the proposed legislation or send it to a Joint Parliamentary Committee. Foreign funding should not be viewed with automatic suspicion, she stated during her remarks. Sule also commented on youth protests and disputes over political party symbols. The NCP (SP) leader awaits a hearing on the party's legal battle.

stories.title: Explainer: What changes as Parliament passes Registration of Births and Deaths Bill
Color-changing packaging flags meat spoilage before it’s visible
JPSC, E20, anti-reservation: The issues India is talking about
A Swedish couple moved into the dream home in Malmö; three years later, they left it behind for a rural home in Japan
stories.summary: After recently selling their newly constructed home in Sweden, a Swedish couple has made the bold decision to embrace a fresh start by purchasing an empty residence in Japan. This significant change stems from their evolving family aspirations and a burgeoning affection for Asia. They are now excited to undertake renovations on their Japanese abode while immersing themselves in the enchanting culture and scenery of Japan.

stories.title: Flesh-eating bacteria kill 5 in Louisiana, health officials warn beachgoers as all cases are linked to seawater
Who is Sunder Katwala? Indian-origin writer appointed to UK community funding body
21 of 57 TN MPs attend CM Vijay’s meet, reject Delimitation Bill; DMK, AIADMK stay away
India to recover 'Green Boots' climber's body from Everest after 30 years: Report
'We stand in solidarity': CJP delegation reaches Ranchi to support students protesting JPSC, JSSC exams
US Democrats eye probes into Trump-linked firms over impeachment if they regain House control: Report
stories.summary: In a significant move, US House Democrats are gearing up for extensive investigations into the business practices of the Trump administration. Their strategy involves utilizing hearings and subpoenas to scrutinize decisions made that may have led to personal gains. Major corporations such as Apple and Alphabet might find themselves under examination for their regulatory and contractual engagements.

stories.title: 'End this war': Senate Democrats turn up heat on Trump, seek end to Iran hostilities
stories.summary: Democrats introduced a resolution to end unauthorized US military involvement against Iran. Senator John Hickenlooper leads the effort, citing constitutional war powers. This move escalates a congressional challenge to President Donald Trump's handling of the conflict. Military leaders privately advise seeking an off-ramp from ongoing air operations. President Trump expresses confidence that the confrontation could end soon.

stories.title: Utah wildfire: Helicopter with 2 onboard crashes while fighting massive blaze
'Which freedom fighter received most severe punishment?' Kerala orders probe into Savarkar quiz
stories.summary: A school quiz question in Kerala has ignited a political controversy. The question asked about the freedom fighter receiving the most severe British punishment. General education minister N Samsudheen ordered an inquiry into the unauthorized quiz. Opposition parties accused the government of promoting a Sangh Parivar agenda. Officials are investigating who prepared and conducted the quiz.

stories.title: American entrepreneur says 'I'm shocked but honestly not surprised' as US plans to remove 60-day grace period for H-1Bs
'Army safeguarding territory': Arunachal CM Pema Khandu rejects Chinese encroachment
Evening newswrap: Mayawati hits Akhilesh over 'Pandit' twist in SP's PDA formula; IT ministry asks Meta to revamp algorithms & more
Syrian spy chief accused of 2015 'Children's Massacre' hiding in Moscow: Report
Korean proverb of the day and its lessons: 'If you don't walk today, you must run tomorrow'
A new Kansas law now bars students from accessing phones, earbuds and smartwatches all school day
stories.summary: Many states are banning smartphones in schools due to growing distractions and health concerns. Some districts now restrict student phone access from morning bell to afternoon dismissal. Parents are increasingly supporting these bans, citing research and developmental appropriateness. Concerns also focus on excessive screen time and inappropriate content accessed on school devices. Schools are now reviewing technology policies and limiting device usage during non-instructional periods.

stories.title: SAD backs women's quota, delimitation bills after Badal-PM Modi meet fuels buzz
stories.summary: Shiromani Akali Dal has expressed strong support for the prompt enactment of the women's reservation bill, emphasizing the need for fair delimitation to ensure equitable state representation. This advocacy follows a meeting between party president Sukhbir Singh Badal and Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Speculation is rife regarding a potential electoral partnership between SAD and BJP, particularly as both parties have faced declining influence in Punjab's political landscape.

stories.title: 56 decomposing bodies found at Chicago funeral home; owner’s licence suspended
Senate confirms Trump’s ex-lawyer Todd Blanche as US Attorney General
Colorado teen Jude Kofie taught himself piano at 10; now his debut album is out after $15,000 gift
stories.summary: Colorado teenager Jude Kofie has released his debut album, showcasing his piano skills. He taught himself to play the piano by ear at age ten. A generous piano tuner gifted him a valuable instrument and professional lessons. His album features diverse musical styles, including jazz and gospel influences. This release marks a significant milestone in his developing musical career.

stories.title: IT ministry asks Meta to revamp algorithms, submit roadmap to tackle deepfakes
'Congress not realising own errors': Rijiju draws parallel with Indira Gandhi post Emergency
stories.summary: Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju criticized the Congress party for its perceived lack of self-awareness. He contrasted the current leadership with former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's admission of Emergency actions. Rahul Gandhi questioned the delay in implementing the Women's Reservation Bill. He urged its immediate implementation without linking it to delimitation. The bill's passage and subsequent implementation remain a point of contention.

stories.title: Greenland issues ‘strong warning’ over Arctic drilling by Trump-linked firm
stories.summary: A US oil firm has moved equipment to Greenland without local approval. This action occurs while President Trump seeks greater US influence over the territory. Greenland's government issued a strong warning regarding the unauthorized logistical operation. The company plans to drill for oil, which faces environmental and political questions. The situation highlights Greenland's resource development authority amid US strategic interests.

stories.title: 'A morning I will cherish': Raghav Chadha's first social media post with PM Modi
Congress lost the millennials. Can it win over Gen Z?
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi is focusing on forging a bond with the youth ahead of the 2029 elections, recognizing that Gen Z will be a key voting bloc.

stories.title: US Senate passes stopgap funding bill to avert shutdown ahead of midterms
stories.summary: In a decisive move, the US Senate has passed a temporary spending bill aimed at funding government operations until December eleventh. This crucial legislation is designed to avert a government shutdown just before the midterm elections. Key components of the bill address border patrol funding as requested by Democrats and extend the deadline for enforcing a federal prohibition on certain hemp products by a month.

stories.title: 10-year-old baker's grand champion cake fetches $15,000 at Maryland county fair auction
stories.summary: At a recent county fair auction, a remarkable cake created by 10-year-old baker Herbie Martin IV fetched an astounding $15,000. Herbie dedicated countless late-night hours to master his delightful lemon blueberry recipe. This impressive sale contributed to an overall fundraising goal, raising more than $100,000 for upcoming fairs and youth initiatives, with Herbie's cake standing out as the highlight of the event.

stories.title: Green Bank Radio Restrictions: Tiny US town lives under radio-silence laws
US officials will not release cool water from Glen Canyon Dam this year, protecting hydropower while threatening humpback chub
stories.summary: This year, federal officials have decided against releasing cool water from the Colorado River reservoirs, emphasizing the need for hydropower production over the conservation of a threatened fish species. The river and its reservoirs are facing severe depletion from overuse and climate change, while states have been unable to reach a long-term agreement on water sharing. Utilities welcomed this choice, citing concerns over the costs of alternative energy sources.

stories.title: 'Changing colours like a chameleon': Mayawati hits Akhilesh over 'Pandit' twist in SP's PDA formula
stories.summary: BSP chief Mayawati criticized the Samajwadi Party's changing political stance. She accused the SP of altering its PDA formula for electoral gains. Mayawati stated the SP now targets Brahmin voters after noticing BSP's growing support. She urged all communities to remain vigilant against SP's casteist politics. Such deceptive strategies offer short-term benefits but not societal welfare.

stories.title: US Fire Service In Antarctica: Frozen desert fuels fire risk
Researchers map 100+ lakes in Brazil, Uruguay that could warn of ecosystem collapse
Zebra mussels are collapsing structures and pipes in Spain's Ebro River since 2001 with a population of 40,000 per square meter
stories.summary: Zebra mussels are proliferating swiftly in Spain's aquatic systems, resulting in considerable harm to infrastructure and creating disturbances in water supply. Experts advocate that modifying infrastructure represents the only effective long-term remedy. The mere removal of adult mussels fails to address the persistent issue of shell buildup.
