The healthcare system is being transformed through AI-driven diagnostics, and access to government services is increasing. Furthermore, AI contributes to strengthening climate resilience and streamlining agricultural loan assessments, prompting significant investments in the necessary infrastructure.

stories.title: Security on high alert in Jammu & Kashmir: Pakistani drone sighted in Kathua, anti-terror search intensifies in Poonch
stories.summary: A Pakistani drone was spotted over Kathua's Hiranagar sector, prompting a security search. Security forces also conducted a large anti-terror operation in Poonch district. An unexploded mortar shell was recovered from a house in Kathua. These events occur amid heightened tensions along the India-Pakistan border. India stated it will safeguard its national interests as needed.

stories.title: Meet Darshan Magdum, Indian member of US boy band, who finally gets O-1 visa and the Internet is behind it
Iran war depletes US missile stocks, raises concerns over readiness for China
Delhi SIR dates extended: BLO visits till August 17, final rolls on October 27
How the US army built the 1,500-mile Alaska Highway in just 8 months
Hidden for 2,000 years, this Egyptian tomb held 560 ushabti figurines meant to serve the dead in the afterlife
stories.summary: Excavations at Tell Quesna have revealed a remarkable funerary complex adorned with hundreds of burial artifacts. Among the treasures, archaeologists discovered 560 ushabti figurines, believed to assist the deceased in the afterlife. Additional finds included protective amulets and pottery, with imported items from Rhodes highlighting trade links with the Mediterranean. These artifacts significantly enhance our knowledge of ancient Egyptian spiritual beliefs and rituals.

stories.title: When Jeff Bezos asked his team to help after a rainforest charity saving the Amazon said it was blocked from using 'Amazon' in Google Ads
What is 'Operation Fortress'? Reform UK's military plan to stop migrants crossing English Channel
'RSS involvement in Sainik Schools increasing', says Rahul Gandhi; Parl panel chief demands evidence
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi alleged increasing RSS involvement in Sainik Schools during a committee meeting. He referred to a media report while making his claim to the panel. The committee chair asked Rahul Gandhi to provide supporting documents for his allegations. Other BJP members also questioned the basis of his statements. Gandhi has previously accused the RSS of capturing public institutions.

stories.title: ‘Why the hurry?' Punjab Assembly opposes E20 policy, alleges Centre acted under US pressure
stories.summary: Punjab's Assembly passed a resolution opposing the Centre's E20 fuel policy. Concerns were raised about potential vehicle damage from the higher ethanol blend. The state questioned the accelerated rollout and alleged external pressure influenced the decision. The Aam Aadmi Party is campaigning nationwide against the policy. They demand consumer choice and lower prices for the blended fuel.

stories.title: How John Beal transformed polluted Hamm Creek into a thriving salmon habitat
stories.summary: John Beal, a dedicated Vietnam veteran, took it upon himself to revive Seattle's Hamm Creek, which had suffered from pollution. His approach included removing trash and reintroducing native plants to restore the ecosystem. By founding I'M A PAL, Beal rallied local volunteers and secured necessary funding, reigniting community passion. His perseverance has led to Hamm Creek's reintegration with the Duwamish River, fostering rich wildlife and ensuring a lasting ecological legacy.

stories.title: Udhayanidhi Stalin arrest drama: 'No double meaning in my speech; TN CM using diversion tactic,' says DMK leader - top developments
stories.summary: Udhayanidhi Stalin faced arrest over alleged remarks linked to actor Trisha. The Madras High Court directed his release on station bail after questioning. DMK workers staged protests across Tamil Nadu following the arrest. The TVK government and opposition engaged in a war of words. Udhayanidhi denied allegations and stated his remarks were distorted.

stories.title: Only 4 companies? Critics say barring small companies from hiring H-1B for 1-2 years is not enough
'Madrassa pass-outs develop terrorist-like mindset': UP deputy CM Keshav Maurya
stories.summary: Speaking to reporters at Vidhan Bhavan, Maurya alleged that madrassa students do not express patriotic slogans and linked their education to extremism. "Anyone who receives a madrassa education does not chant 'Bharat Mata Ki Jai' nor sing 'Vande Mataram', and develops a terrorist-like mindset," he was quoted as saying by news agency PTI. The remarks were strongly criticised by senior Samajwadi Party leader Shivpal Yadav.

stories.title: California's Ranch fire burned 459,123 acres; 8 years later, 71,000 seedlings have been planted
stories.summary: Eight years after California's devastating Ranch Fire burned more than 459,000 acres, the US Forest Service and partner organisations planted 71,000 conifer seedlings in just eight days. The reforestation effort is part of a long-term plan to restore damaged forest, reduce future wildfire risk and support natural recovery across the Mendocino National Forest.

stories.title: How people in Chile's Atacama Desert evolved to survive drinking arsenic-poisoned water
Scientists discover Greenland sharks can see for centuries, debunking blindness myth
stories.summary: Recent studies reveal that Greenland sharks possess well-preserved visual systems that can last for centuries, challenging the previous notion that they were nearly blind. Research shows that their eyes are uniquely suited for low-light environments, demonstrating impressive adaptability. Scientists found healthy rod cells and active genes responsible for light detection, indicating these sharks have a remarkable ability to maintain their eyesight throughout their extended lifespans.

stories.title: Dordoi Bazaar: Shipping container market to commercial heart of Central Asia
'Private media entity organising it': Govt says 'no role' in Sheikh Hasina's proposed August 5 event
stories.summary: The MEA stated no government involvement in a private media event. The proposed forum concerns former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. Bangladesh sought clarification from India regarding its support for the event. Hasina resigned in August 2024 and has been living in Delhi. She faces a death sentence for crimes against humanity.

stories.title: 'Insult to nation': Mamata attacks BJP over Netaji remarks, alleges pressure on TMC leaders
'Who is PM Modi to forgive?' Rahul says students 'need apology not forgiveness'
stories.summary: In an Instagram video posted on Friday night PM said that he will forgive young protesters accused of abusing him and his late mother, saying they are misguided children and it is “our job to show them the right way” “Nothing is more painful than seeing a parent grieve their child. Behind every young life lost is a family carrying pain that will never leave them - and serious questions about a broken education system,” Gandhi said in a post on X where he also shared images of his interaction with parents and students.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Giorgia Meloni: "To the women of this nation I want to say that being underestimated is a great advantage, because…”
North Carolina man worked 100-hour weeks for 58 years to save a bankrupt boat company, rejected a $400 million offer and gave it to charity
SC orders nationwide action against 'digital arrest' scams; tells RBI to share SOP on 'mule accounts'
'Answered public discontent with bullets and repression': MEA slams Pakistan over 'farce' PoK polls
stories.summary: In a strong statement, the Ministry of External Affairs demanded action against cross-border terrorism, directly targeting groups like Lashkar-e-Taiba following claims about Indian agencies taking down their commanders. They lambasted the local elections in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir as illegitimate, citing repression of civilians by Pakistani forces. Moreover, India urged the global community to address Pakistan's actions firmly.

stories.title: 'Will do whatever is necessary for national interest': India after Pakistan deploys 250 Chinese Howitzers
stories.summary: India stated it will protect national interests after Pakistan deployed Chinese artillery guns. Pakistan has reportedly deployed around 250 Chinese-made SH-15 artillery systems. India criticized Pakistan's recent elections in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir as a farce. The spokesperson noted civilian deaths during a crackdown in the region. Both nations continue to modernize their respective artillery capabilities.

stories.title: Evening newswrap: Madras HC orders Udhayanidhi's release after arrest over 'double meaning' remark; flyers injured as Air India's Phuket-Delhi flight encounters turbulence & more
Travel planning India's most underappreciated vacation task: Survey
Scottish biotech company turned whisky waste into a source of omega-3
Scientists find slugs, beetles and crabs help spread seeds for 186 plant species
'Gungi gudiya' row: NCP workers barge into Maharashtra Congress office over remark on deputy CM Sunetra Pawar — watch
'Decisions at appropriate time': Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren breaks silence on recruitment row amid protests
stories.summary: Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren addressed recruitment row concerns seriously. Protesting job aspirants demand an independent probe into examination irregularities. The state CID investigation is gathering pace with several arrests made. Former CM Raghubar Das urged dialogue and a CBI inquiry for justice. The indefinite sit-in continues, with protesters vowing to escalate their agitation.

stories.title: Biodiversity boosts forest growth; loss could cut gains 17% by 2050
'Sadhu-saint not involved': CM Yogi on Ram Mandir donation theft case
stories.summary: Addressing reporters, CM Yogi said said the initial SIT report had not found any involvement of religious figures in the alleged theft of offerings made at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple. "No involvement of any sadhu-saint was found in the SIT's initial report in the case related to the alleged embezzlement of offerings (chadhava) at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple," he said.

stories.title: More than 330,000 gallons of rotting fish sauce in a Canadian town are finally being removed after 20 years of unbearable stench
Quote of the day by Princess Diana: "Don't call me an icon. I'm just a mother trying to…"
How Korea's Haenyeo developed extraordinary cold resistance that lets them dive into near-freezing seas without oxygen tanks, even in their 70s
When wildfires make their own weather: As France sees its first fire cloud, should India be worried?
stories.summary: France witnessed its first pyrocumulonimbus fire cloud event in July 2026. This phenomenon occurs when intense wildfires create their own thunderstorms. India's rising temperatures and dry spells increase forest fire frequency. While India has not reported fire clouds, its forests are becoming more flammable. The Himalayan pine belt presents the highest potential for such an event in India.

stories.title: Andrew Tate's lawyer warns Trump of political fallout if he doesn't help jailed influencer in UK extradition case
How Felix Dennis launched a 10 million-tree vision to restore England's woodlands
stories.summary: Felix Dennis began planting a small wood in 1996, which grew into the Heart of England Forest. This project aimed to restore native broadleaf trees across South Warwickshire. The charity was established in 2003 to continue purchasing and planting land. Dennis envisioned 25,000 acres of woodland open to the public. After his death in 2014, the forest has expanded significantly.

stories.title: Scientists discover four dangerous fish bacteria in Brazil for the first time; one has jumped to a new host species
stories.summary: For the first time, Brazil faces a significant challenge as bacteria previously exclusive to Asia and the USA have been identified within its borders. These bacteria, known to cause columnaris disease, pose an acute risk to the thriving aquaculture sector. Researchers have isolated four species from the Flavobacterium genus, which can infect both Nile tilapia and indigenous fish species.

stories.title: Arrested Jaish suspect surveyed area near CM Suvendu Adhikari's residence: Official
'Many friends yet to return': Patna students restart protest over NEET stir crackdown
stories.summary: The demonstrators demanded immediate release of all students still in jail and the withdrawal of criminal cases registered against those arrested during the statewide agitation. "We want a verified list of those who have been released from jail and those who are still behind bars after being arrested during the protests," one of the protesters said. A student activist from Siwan also alleged excessive use of force during earlier protests.

stories.title: Ancient Roman women left more than 120 inscriptions inside a hidden cave in Spain dedicated to a mysterious goddess
Scientists warn Earth could hit the 1.5°C climate limit sooner than expected
stories.summary: Global warming has significantly accelerated, with the past decade warming faster than any comparable period. Researchers removed natural climate fluctuations to reveal this underlying warming trend. Five major global temperature datasets confirm this acceleration with high statistical confidence. This observed increase suggests the world may approach key climate thresholds sooner. The long-term trend could cross the Paris Agreement's 1.5°C limit before this decade ends.

stories.title: Iran won't escalate tensions but will defend itself, says Pezeshkian amid Trump's warning
stories.summary: Iran states it will defend its security while the US president claims a last chance for a deal. Conflicting reports emerge regarding ongoing negotiations between Iran and the United States. Shipping activity through the Strait of Hormuz remains subdued amid these diplomatic claims. Iran's IRGC reportedly launched a drone attack on a US military base in Kuwait. Tehran also prepared retaliatory strikes on Ukraine after a vessel incident.

stories.title: Madras HC orders Udhayanidhi Stalin's release after arrest over 'double meaning' remark
World's oldest amber has been found in China, and it is 65 million years older than expected
stories.summary: In a remarkable discovery, scientists uncovered ancient amber specimens in China that are approximately 385 million years old. This significant find pushes the amber fossil record back by an impressive sixty-five million years. It indicates that early vascular plants may have developed advanced resin-producing capabilities, which could have provided a defensive advantage against wildfires and fungal diseases. The research advances our understanding of plant resilience during the Devonian era.

stories.title: Countries with most black mambas: From South Africa to Kenya, where the deadly snake is found
stories.summary: The black mamba, often cited as the most dangerous snake on the African continent, occupies a wide array of habitats. This snake thrives in arid savannas and rocky terrains throughout sub-Saharan Africa. Countries such as South Africa and Zimbabwe frequently report incidents of black mamba bites. Remarkably, sightings have increased in Kenya and Zambia at higher altitudes, with Tanzania and Botswana also within its expansive territory.

stories.title: Scientists in Iceland are turning carbon dioxide into stone by injecting it into volcanic rock, and it could redefine the fight against climate change
Europe's shrinking rivers have hit shipping, power and tourism
stories.summary: Record low water levels in Europe's major rivers are disrupting electricity production, cargo transport and business operations as heatwaves and drought continue across the continent. Nuclear and hydropower plants have cut output, shipping on the Danube and Rhine has slowed, and companies are reporting lower earnings, highlighting the growing economic impact of prolonged extreme weather

stories.title: Long before GPS, Polynesian sailors crossed the Pacific by reading stars, waves, winds, birds and clouds
Sudden drop in altitude: Flyers injured as Air India's Phuket-Delhi flight encounters turbulence
Mark Zuckerberg's wife invested $125 million in a school for the disadvantaged; now she is closing it to focus on AI
stories.summary: The Primary School, offering tuition-free education to low-income families, has officially closed, impacting around 540 children who depended on its support. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, the school's benefactor, is redirecting its resources towards biotechnology and artificial intelligence. As part of its commitment, it has announced substantial funding aimed at assisting affected students and local organizations.

stories.title: Rose-ringed parakeets: From escaped pets to one of the most recognisable birds
AAP protest E20 petrol policy: Kejriwal, Sisodia stage sit-in after march to PM Modi's residence stopped
stories.summary: Delhi Police stopped Arvind Kejriwal and AAP leaders marching to Prime Minister Modi's residence. Delhi-NCR led the nation in transplant procedures, while Tamil Nadu topped deceased organ donors. India now ranks third globally in total organ transplants, after the US and China. The questionnaire for this significant census phase will be notified soon.

stories.title: 60 venomous snakes, cocaine, guns and 22,000 dollars in cash seized during New Mexico drug raid

stories.summary: The Supreme Court has extended legal protection to live-in relationships. These relationships are now covered under Section 498A of the IPC. The court stated that the law must adapt to changing societal norms. Cruelty within such relationships will now be punishable by law. This decision aims to protect women from domestic violence and harassment.

stories.title: Quote by Ludwig Wittgenstein: 'The real question of life after death isn't whether or not it exists...'
stories.summary: Philosopher Ludwig Wittgenstein challenged the preoccupation with life after death, suggesting that eternal existence does not address the fundamental questions of life’s meaning. His reflections emerged amidst the chaos of World War One. In contemporary discussions on digital immortality, this crucial insight often gets overshadowed; authentic meaning resides in fully embracing the present and living with intention.

stories.title: Quote of the day by JS Mill: 'I have learned to seek my happiness by limiting my desires...'
stories.summary: Victorian philosopher John Stuart Mill believed that true happiness lies in limiting our desires rather than endlessly pursuing them. After facing a mental crisis due to his upbringing, Mill shifted his philosophy, warning that unending desire leads to a hedonic treadmill. Today, our consumer-driven culture reflects this endless chase; by curbing material wishes, we can unlock a wealth of inner fulfillment and deeper contentment.

stories.title: The tiny helicopter Nasa built to survive 30 days on Mars ended up flying for nearly three years
In 2016, nations created the world's largest marine reserve in Antarctica
stories.summary: The Ross Sea Marine Protected Area became a global conservation milestone after years of negotiation. This vast Antarctic reserve was established by the CCAMLR member states in 2016. It protects a significant marine ecosystem supporting diverse wildlife and vital phytoplankton blooms. Scientific study of climate change impacts is also a key benefit of this protected area. However, limitations exist regarding fishing and the reserve's 35-year lifespan.

stories.title: Kerala rain fury: 15 dead, 7 missing as relief camps shelter thousands
How J. Robert Oppenheimer brought together thousands of scientists to build the world's first atomic bomb
'Entire system working to protect Brij Bhushan': Vinesh Phogat says wrestlers to continue fight
Who is Jacob Tsimerman: Fields Medal-winning mathematics professor who was once one of AI's biggest critics, now joining OpenAI to tackle AI safety
Only three Hawaiian producers meet US's organic honey standards; study suggests rule review
stories.summary: A new study found that organically managed bee colonies on farms in the northeastern US produced honey with pesticide residue levels comparable to certified organic honey. Researchers say current US organic certification rules may be stricter than necessary, but caution that more studies across different regions are needed before any nationwide policy changes.

stories.title: Scientists claim the shrinking Pacific Ocean will lead to the formation of a new supercontinent 'Amasia'
stories.summary: The Pacific Ocean, which is the largest ocean on Earth, is gradually shrinking due to the convergence of tectonic plates. Subduction zones around its edges are consuming the ocean floor at a rate faster than new material is formed. Scientists estimate that in 200 to 300 million years, the Pacific could entirely close up, pulling continents together to create a new supercontinent.

stories.title: Jantar Mantar no longer ideal location for protest site? SC hears PIL seeking alternative venue
Karnataka Cabinet set for major expansion today; 20 ministers to take oath - Full list
Scientists survey Mount Ararat glacier to recover its first ice core
stories.summary: A German-Turkish research team has completed the first scientific survey of the glacier on Mount Ararat, Turkey's highest peak, to study its potential as a record of climate and human history. Scientists mapped the shrinking ice cap to identify the best site for drilling the mountain's first ice core, hoping it will reveal thousands of years of environmental and archaeological information before melting erases it.

stories.title: Parliament panel to meet social media platforms over online safety, privacy
Scientists solve the 100-year-old mystery behind why avocado flowers change sex over two days
Meet the General Grant Tree: The world's second-largest tree that became America's only living National Shrine
stories.summary: The General Grant Tree stands as the world's second-largest tree by volume. It became America's National Christmas Tree in nineteen twenty-six. President Dwight D. Eisenhower declared it a living National Shrine in nineteen fifty-six. This sequoia honors men and women who served the nation. Its size and history make it a remarkable natural landmark.

stories.title: Raji Doshi, 12, designed an algae system to reduce ocean acidity; now eyes $25,000 science prize
stories.summary: A young student from Connecticut is a finalist in a science competition for her innovative project. Her project proposes using algae and natural calcium buffers to reduce ocean acidification. This innovative idea could help protect vulnerable marine organisms from acidic conditions. She is competing for a substantial grand prize and valuable scientific mentorship. Her work highlights the significant contributions young minds can make to environmental solutions.

stories.title: Pacific trend raised US Southwest wildfire area 22%, cut Australia’s 19%
stories.summary: A Pacific Ocean warming trend has impacted wildfire conditions globally. This pattern amplified fire risks in the southwestern United States significantly. Conversely, it eased fire conditions in eastern Australia during the study. Researchers analyzed decades of wildfire and climate data for these findings. Understanding these ocean-climate links can improve future wildfire forecasts.

stories.title: Nearly 81 years after Hiroshima, scientists discover a hidden metal alloy created by the atomic bomb blast
stories.summary: Scientists found a new metallic alloy in Hiroshima shoreline sand. This alloy formed from extreme heat and rapid cooling during the 1945 atomic blast. Researchers identified its unique chemical makeup and crystal structure in microscopic particles. The discovery offers insights into matter behavior under extreme conditions. This finding could inspire future materials science research and nuclear forensics.

stories.title: 'Would have hanged myself if guilty': Brij Bhushan after acquittal in wrestlers' sexual harassment case
stories.summary: A Delhi court acquitted former WFI chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and Vinod Tomar. Singh stated he always believed justice would be served and "never felt guilty". He reiterated his claim that the allegations were part of a conspiracy against him. The court acquitted both individuals after reviewing the chargesheet.

stories.title: Mississippi man uncovers more than 200 Civil War cannonballs buried beneath his property after 160 years
Live-in partners can seek protection under Section 498A, says Supreme Court
Meet Nathan Thomas: 18-year-old Florida teen becomes the world's youngest male professor after breaking a 306-year-old record
Celebrities who were practising doctors before they became famous
stories.summary: Many doctors have pursued alternative careers, finding success in creative fields. Michael Crichton became a renowned author and screenwriter after medical school. Ken Jeong transitioned from internal medicine to a popular acting career. Khaled Hosseini became a best-selling author after practicing medicine. Che Guevara and Sir Arthur Conan Doyle also left medicine for significant impact.

stories.title: Kunal Kamra shifts three Whitefield shows following opposition by 'Hindutva activists'
​From cancer survivors to surfing stars: California woman and her dog beat cancer before competing together at the World Dog Surfing Championships
A race to save 23 sperms, and a teen cancer survivor’s chance at fatherhood
2 strategic satellites sit at spaceport as govt nod eludes Isro
stories.summary: India's space ambitions face a setback as all launches are paused pending governmental clearance. The NVS-03 and Gisat-1A satellites are primed for their missions, but concerns have surfaced after two recent PSLV mission failures, casting shadows over the launch schedule. Experts express confusion over the decision to delay launches of seemingly unrelated rockets. To date, the government has not released an extensive analysis of past mission issues.

stories.title: Fans Split Over Self-Mural: Clavicular penthouse photo sparks debate; critics see dictator narcissism, others defend art
stories.summary: Clavicular sparked a social media storm after a photo of a massive self-portrait mural inside his penthouse went viral. Many fans mocked the artwork, comparing it to a dictator-style portrait, while others defended it as an impressive artistic choice. The online debate quickly filled with jokes, criticism, and praise, turning the mural into a trending topic and leaving social media sharply divided over its meaning and symbolism.

stories.title: MP Pappu Yadav attacked at home during presser
stories.summary: An independent MP, Pappu Yadav, faced an alleged attack during a news conference. A man threw a slipper while another reportedly brandished a knife at the event. The incident is believed to be linked to his recent protest outside Parliament. Police have detained one suspect and are investigating the other's involvement. The MP's team claims he had received prior death threats.

stories.title: New Evidence In D4vd Case: Prosecutors cite texts and forensics at hearing; defense contests proof
stories.summary: Prosecutors presented alleged text messages and forensic evidence in the D4vd murder case, claiming the singer had a secret relationship with 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez. Burke has pleaded not guilty, while the defense challenged key evidence during the preliminary hearing. Trial proceedings are expected to continue later this year.

stories.title: Highway deaths dip in India for 1st time since Covid
Charlie Kirk Assassination Case: Candace Owens questions FBI timeline; casts doubt on evidence
stories.summary: Candace Owens has questioned the FBI's response timeline in the Charlie Kirk murder investigation, asking why agents arrived at Utah Valley University so quickly. She also challenged key parts of the prosecution's case against Tyler Robinson, including the evidence presented and the official account of the shooting, while continuing to raise doubts about the federal investigation.

stories.title: Youth quitting drugs real warriors: PM on national drive
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi launched a campaign for drug-free youth for a developed India. He emphasized that families should seek expert help and foster open communication. Youth overcoming addiction are considered warriors and deserve societal respect and second chances. Enemy nations use drug supply as part of terror plans targeting the country's future. The campaign will run for 100 weeks, organizing various de-addiction activities.

stories.title: NTA floats tender to secure offices, exam material 24x7
10,000 cases pending in SC for 10 yrs, 80,000 in HCs for 30 yrs
stories.summary: Despite significant investment, court infrastructure and technology have not reduced decades-old case pendency. Over ten thousand cases remain pending in the Supreme Court for more than ten years. High courts across India have over eighty thousand cases pending for over three decades. The law minister cited judicial responsibility and judicial vacancies as reasons for the delays. New laws and committees have been established to address the growing backlog of cases.

stories.title: Congress set to stall House over Ram temple donation scam
TVK & Congress not on same page on Cauvery
DMK slams Congress for 'trading trust for berths'
stories.summary: DMK fiercely responded to Rahul Gandhi's criticism of supporting a bill to increase Lok Sabha seats. Senior DMK MP Dayanidhi Maran accused Congress of betraying trust for ministerial positions. The BJP hopes DMK's anger with Congress will aid its legislative agenda. DMK has indicated openness to the bill after studying its impact. Rahul Gandhi's comments acknowledge the possibility of DMK revising its stance on the bill.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Cicero: 'If we are not ashamed to think it, we should not be ashamed to say it'
stories.summary: Cicero, the Roman statesman, passionately argued for the alignment of one's thoughts with spoken words, critiquing the harmful effects of self-censorship. He posited that institutions become vulnerable when necessary truths go unspoken, a lesson still applicable in today's workplaces and government. The consequences of silence can be dire, stifling effective problem-solving. Open dialogue is essential for maintaining integrity and avoiding misguided decisions.

stories.title: Sun Pharma withdraws 11 eye medicines
SC warns Punjab for ignoring 15-yr-old ruling on dues to Himachal Pradesh
stories.summary: The Supreme Court criticized Punjab for its resistance to implementing an old decree. Attorney General Venkataramani proposed a cashless settlement for power dues. Himachal and Haryana agreed to the proposal, while Punjab raised objections. The court warned Punjab of consequences if it fails to comply. A final decision is expected on August 12.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Homer: 'Of all creatures that breathe and move upon the earth, nothing is...'
stories.summary: Homer's Odyssey explores the delicate balance of human existence, revealing how unpredictability shapes our lives. The ancient Greeks regarded people as ephemeroi—fleeting beings, a stark contrast to the enduring gods. This perspective remains significant today, as seen in the volatility of financial markets and professional sports, where fortunes fluctuate rapidly. Embracing our vulnerabilities can lead to humility and more effective planning.

stories.title: US scientists analysed 55 storm and atmospheric variables to identify hurricane rapid intensification
stories.summary: Coastal communities might soon benefit from enhanced hurricane forecasting. A groundbreaking statistical model predicts rapid hurricane intensification up to five days in advance, significantly improving early warnings. This innovation analyzes a multitude of environmental factors, allowing forecasters to anticipate dangerous storm developments with increased accuracy, ultimately safeguarding lives and property from unexpected hurricane threats.

stories.title: 'Cancel JPSC exam': Jharkhand students continue protest, seek CBI investigation
Israel, US military learnt Trump cancelled Iran strike through social media: Report
'2024 movement fooled Bangladesh': Taslima Nasreen's 'lesson' warning over Delhi student protests
stories.summary: Exiled author Taslima Nasreen believes Bangladesh's student movement misled people. She drew parallels between past protests and recent demonstrations in Delhi. Nasreen stated that Islamic fundamentalists were behind the Bangladesh movement. This experience reinforced her concerns about the consequences of such actions. The developments in Bangladesh should serve as a cautionary lesson for others.

stories.title: UK PM Burnham may exempt child sex offenders from early release scheme
Hungary shut its only nuclear plant for the first time in 44 years
stories.summary: Hungary's sole nuclear facility has been offline due to unprecedentedly low levels of the Danube River. This shutdown exacerbates power shortages amid a fierce summer heatwave, prompting the government to urge both households and businesses to conserve energy. Consequently, Hungary must depend on costly electricity imports from neighboring countries, highlighting the fragility of energy systems in the face of severe weather changes.

stories.title: 'Cruel terrorist act': Moscow mayor on restaurant blast that killed 3, injured 21
Brazilian scientists sampled 800 trees across 63 Amazon locations; their atomic fingerprinting...
stories.summary: Brazilian scientists are innovating with an isotopic mapping model designed to tackle illegal logging head-on. This novel forensic tool examines atomic signatures within trees, allowing them to trace the origination of timber effectively. Currently, the model can eliminate ninety-two percent of the Amazon rainforest from potential illegal wood sources, utilizing stable isotope analysis for secure chemical fingerprinting. The goal is to bolster law enforcement investigations and diminish global timber crime.

stories.title: Ex-nurse revives baby who stopped breathing during Arizona post-office visit
stories.summary: A former nurse's quick actions saved an infant's life at an Arizona post office. Mary Schwarz performed CPR and airway clearing on baby Nova who stopped breathing. Police Lieutenant Shari Aguilar then transported the infant to a nearby clinic for immediate medical attention. Nova, who had prior heart issues, began breathing again during the car ride. This incident highlights the critical importance of CPR training in everyday situations.

stories.title: 9,000 discarded Christmas trees help restore New Orleans wetlands
stories.summary: New Orleans is giving used Christmas trees a second life by dropping them into coastal marshes to help slow land loss. The bundled trees trap sediment, reduce wave energy and support marsh grass growth. Scientists say the method helps restore wetlands in selected areas but is only one part of Louisiana's broader coastal protection efforts.

stories.title: US general warns Pentagon he lacks naval assets to keep shielding Israel from missiles: Report
Ramlila body asks 'Ramayana' makers to hold special screening before release, warns of protests
stories.summary: The Shri Ramlila Mahasangh requested a special preview screening of the upcoming Ramayana film. This demand aims to prevent any scenes that might offend Hindu sentiments. The organization warned of protests if their preview request is not accepted. The film's trailer features Ranbir Kapoor as Rama and Yash as Ravana. Ramayana: Part 1 is scheduled for a Diwali 2026 release.

stories.title: Educated but unemployed: Inside India's broken jobs market and why the 'cockroaches' are fed up
stories.summary: India's expanding higher education system produces millions of graduates annually. However, quality job creation has not kept pace with this educational growth. Many educated youth struggle to find stable, well-paying employment opportunities. This mismatch fuels widespread frustration and youth-led protests across the nation. The situation highlights a critical challenge for India's demographic dividend.

stories.title: Researchers mapped 128 million US buildings for landslide exposure; 6.5 million Americans live in...
stories.summary: A recent study identifies millions of Americans at risk from landslide hazards, revealing that densely populated eastern states have higher exposure. The challenges mount for rural communities when recovery from landslides is needed, contrasting with wealthier cities that implement zoning and engineering strategies to minimize risk. The findings stress the importance of increased public investment and disaster aid for rural areas facing these dangers.

stories.title: Wildfires near Bordeaux spark fears of hidden damage to France’s wine
stories.summary: France's worst wildfires in decades now threaten Bordeaux's famed wine production. Smoke taint can subtly damage grapes, affecting taste and value for years. This danger arrives during a sensitive ripening period for the grapes. The wine industry already faces market pressures and export challenges. Climate change poses ongoing threats to this vital agricultural sector.

stories.title: 6-7 and the First World War: How Internet absurdism became Dada's unlikely heir
'Not Korean heart ... counting fingers': Shehzad Poonawalla's swipe at Rahul Gandhi over Gen Z post
stories.summary: Shehzad Poonawalla criticised Rahul Gandhi's recent social media post. He interpreted Gandhi's gesture as counting corruption and bribes daily. Poonawalla accused the Gandhi family of extensive involvement in corruption. Rahul Gandhi had shared a Korean finger heart gesture on Friendship Day. This outreach aimed to connect with younger audiences on social media.

stories.title: In 1925, the world’s first motel opened in California with rooms for $1.25; after closing in 1991...
stories.summary: The iconic site of the world's first motel in San Luis Obispo is now on the market. With various redevelopment options available, buyers are encouraged to re-envision this historic property. Established in 1925 and ceasing operations in 1991, this site presents a unique opportunity to either preserve or transform a piece of hospitality history amidst the recent trend of revitalizing classic motels into boutique experiences.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Barack Obama: "Change will not come if we wait for some other person or some other time. We are the ones..."
'Threw slipper, carried a knife': What we know about attack on Pappu Yadav
Assam floods: 82 dead, 1.78 lakh affected as relief efforts intensify - key points
Virginia students save family from lake during golf tryouts
stories.summary: Three Culpeper teenagers are heroes after rescuing a family whose kayaks overturned. They heard a splash and a child screaming, then immediately acted. The teens swam to the struggling family and brought them safely back to shore. Police and school officials praised their quick thinking and courage. Their actions highlight the importance of immediate response in water emergencies.

stories.title: You can make yourselves ‘luckier’: Science-backed tips to rewire your brain for luck
stories.summary: Cultivating a belief in your own luck can reshape your brain to recognize new opportunities. By documenting moments of serendipity, you start to see that luck is more frequent than originally believed. Individuals branded as unlucky often experience heightened anxiety, which narrows their perspective. In contrast, self-proclaimed lucky individuals expect good things and interact more openly. Ultimately, creating your own luck demands conscious choices and more frequent attempts.

stories.title: Bordeaux vineyards escaped the immediate wildfires, but repeated heatwaves are shrinking...
stories.summary: European vineyards face an early harvest due to prolonged heat and drought conditions. Wildfires across southwestern France and Greece have forced thousands to evacuate their homes. Emergency services continue to battle numerous blazes, particularly in Greece and on Crete. Spain sees some relief as national emergency declarations are lifted in certain areas. Record continent-wide warmth exacerbates fire risks and impacts air quality for millions.

stories.title: ‘Ban on Sheikh Hasina’s Awami League a move against democracy’: Taslima Nasreen
Engineers linked two deep wells through 629°F rock beneath Oregon’s Newberry volcano; the experiment could unlock round-the-clock power without burning fuel
stories.summary: Mazama Energy connected two deep wells reaching 629 degrees Fahrenheit. This marks the world's hottest enhanced geothermal system ever built. The company plans three more wells in 2026 targeting hotter rock. This project aims to unlock superhot rock for cleaner energy production. Geothermal energy could become a significant player in the clean energy mix.
